articleTitle: A Robust Protection Scheme to Identify Ground Faults in DC Ring Microgrid Using Ensemble of LDA Based Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In past years, acceptance of the microgrid has rapidly increased to connect near load centers. Microgrid provides many benefits over traditional power networks. However, main issue in DC microgrid is the fault occurrence due to unhealthy conditions. These can be pole-to-pole and pole-toground faults, bidirectional converter behaviour, change in fault resistance, and dissimilar fault current during grid integrated and islanded mode. In the case of the DC microgrid, the rate of change in current with respect to time is very high. Therefore, protection scheme should be proficient. In this paper, an ensemble of linear discriminant analysis has been proposed to detect fault occurrence in the DC microgrid. Samples of the voltage and current in both modes have been used in protection scheme. In this work, the main tasks are given that are mode detection, fault detection/classification, and analysis of the faulty sections in same operating modes.

articleTitle: A power flow control unit for Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) modes of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming increasingly popular due to their zero emissions and low noise levels, which address environmental and energy issues. With the increasing integration of EVs into the power grid, efficient power conversion systems are essential for bidirectional power flow. This work aims to establish vehicle-to-grid (V2G) integration, and this concept is crucial to balancing energy supply and demand. The bidirectional charger of an Electric Vehicle supports the V2G feature, which can help minimize peak electricity demand. This paper investigates the performance of Dual Active Bridge (DAB) and Buck-Boost converters in Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) modes of electric vehicles using state-of-charge control. The control methodologies for both converters are discussed in detail, focusing on their application in G2V and V2G modes. Simulation results using MATLAB Simulink and experimental data are provided to validate the analysis, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of each converter type in these specific EV applications.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of ANN, Fuzzy MPPT in PV system with Traditional Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This research presents a comparative analysis of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Fuzzy Logic-based MPPT techniques PV systems, evaluating their performance against traditional MPPT algorithms, namely Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance (INC). Solar PV systems require accurate and efficient MPPT methods to extract the maximum possible energy under varying environmental conditions. Conventional procedures like P&O and INC, while widely used for their simplicity, often struggle with issues like oscillations around the maximum power point, slow response under changing irradiance, and inefficiency under partial shading. ANN and Fuzzy MPPT algorithms, being adaptive and intelligent, offer potential advantages, such as faster convergence, better handling of nonlinear conditions, and superior performance in dynamic environmental situations. In this paper, simulations are conducted to assess the tracking efficiency, convergence time, and overall energy output of each method. The results reveal that ANN and Fuzzy-based MPPT outperform traditional procedures, especially in terms of accuracy and adaptability to rapid environmental changes. The findings provide the most effective MPPT techniques for improving the operation of solar PV schemes in real-world applications.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent Symbiotic Organisms Search based Modified Fractional-Order PID Controller for Magnetic Levitation Plant
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A non-integer-order PID controller outperforms its integer-order counterpart in terms of better control when used for either integer-order or non-integer-order systems. However, due to a large number of tunable variables, tuning the FOPID controller is a challenging and complex task. This paper proposes a modified FOPID controller (mFOPID) in such a way as to offer comparable performance with a reduced number of parameters. The proposed modification reduces the tunable variables to three, without compromising the performance. The optimal set of parameters for the proposed controller has been estimated using the multi-agent based symbiotic organisms search (MASOS) algorithm by formulating and optimization problem choosing the objective function to be the root mean square error (RMSE). The performance of MASOS is compared with that of Grey Wolf Optimzer (GWO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The efficacy of the proposed control scheme has been assessed by means of implementing it on a magnetic levitation system (MLP), which is a nonlinear second-order open-loop unstable plant and has been compared with that of integer-order PID (IOPID) and FOPID controllers. The numerical results confirm the enhanced performance of the proposed controller and superiority of MASOS over the other algorithms. It was inferred that the proposed control scheme restricts both settling time and peak overshoot in the closed loop response, by more than 90% when compared to the other controllers. Additionally, the proposed scheme makes the system robust against parameter variations by imparting the isodamping property.

articleTitle: A SPWM Strategy Based Dual-Inverter Control for Electric Vehicle with Open End Winding Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the implementation of a dual 2 -level (2L) voltage source inverter (VSI) to drive an open-end winding induction motor (OEWIM) for electric vehicle (EV) applications. This paper presents a mathematical model of an OEWIM drive, which is powered by dual 2L VSI with separate DC supplies. A sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) strategy is employed, incorporating a phase shift of the carrier wave. By comparing a sinusoidal wave with a triangular signal, this strategy enables the generation of swing states for the two inverters in a spontaneous and symmetrical manner. The proposed configuration offers numerous advantages, including improved efficiency, reduced harmonic distortion, enhanced control capabilities, and fault-tolerant operation. The proposed system is designed to meet the demanding requirements of EVs, such as high torque density, fault tolerant operation, and improved power quality. In this study, through the suggested model utilizing the MATLAB/Simulink platform for analysis and simulation. The performance is validated thought experiments. The proposed model benefits from a robust and versatile environment that enables accurate representation and evaluation of the system’s behavior, performance, and dynamics.

articleTitle: A Computationally Efficient Phasor Measurement using Interpolation DFT for Distribution network
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Phasor measurements become essential for ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of the distribution network, requiring a simple method to measure the phasor with less computational cost. This paper attempts to design and analyse a computationally efficient phasor measurement using interpolated discrete fourier transform (DFT) with the Kaiser function. This interpolated DFT is achieved with three-point interpolation using the least-square polynomial. The performance evaluation of phasor estimation is evaluated according to the compliance tests prescribed in the IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1 standard. The result analysis reveals that the interpolated DFT-based phasor estimation offers appreciable performance compared to the reference model at a lower sampling rate and latency.

articleTitle: Real-Time IoT Driven Energy Monitoring System for Eight Meter Gear Hobbing Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The manufacturing industry heavily depends on gear hobbing machines to produce high-precision gears essential for different sectors like heavy machinery, automotive, aerospace, etc. However, optimizing the energy efficiency of these machines presents a significant challenge. Traditional monitoring systems often fail to deliver real-time data and insights, resulting in inefficiencies, increased operational costs and risk of machine failures. This paper introduces a real-time IoT-driven energy monitoring system developed for Gear-Hobbing machinery to address the above challenges. The systems implementation involves tools like Node-RED for data workflows, MQTT (Message Query Telemetry Transport) Explorer for message tracking, MODSCAN-64 for device communication, and hardware components like the MODBUS TO ETHERNET converter module for data collection. Data is processed and stored in an ORACLE Database, with a front-end interface built using JavaScript and HTML for user interaction. This comprehensive approach gives operators critical insights to improve the machine efficiency and achieve significant cost savings.

articleTitle: Magnetic Levitation Control Using Deep Reinforcement Learning and Prioritized Experience Replay with Action Noise Variations
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In recent years, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a promising approach for addressing control problems in complex, nonlinear environments. The ability of RL algorithms to autonomously learn optimal control policies without requiring an explicit system model makes them particularly suited for real-time applications in fields like robotics and industrial automation. This paper investigates the application of RL algorithms for controlling a magnetic levitation (maglev) system, which presents significant challenges due to its nonlinear dynamics. The Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm and the integration of Prioritized Experience Replay (PER) are employed to enhance learning efficiency. The impact of varying action noise (random perturbations added to actions) for exploration and system performance is explored; results demonstrate that TD3 with PER achieves superior stability, faster convergence, and reduced rise and settling times without overshoot. These findings emphasize the importance of tailored exploration strategies in optimizing control policies for complex environments, highlighting the potential of advanced RL techniques for real-time control applications.

articleTitle: A Dual Switch DC/DC Convertor for Extensive Voltage Conversion Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a common-grounded Unidirectional DC/DC Converter (UDC) designed to provide an extensive voltage conversion, rendering it ideal for diverse applications such as renewable energy systems and electric vehicles. The proposed UDC aims to improve power conversion efficiency while reducing system complexity. By employing a simple, non-isolated UDC, it addresses limitations associated with existing UDC, such as high component count and reduced efficiency at higher voltage levels. The proposed UDC utilizes fewer components compared to conventional designs, which leads to cost-effectiveness. The design allows for an extensive voltage conversion with minimal losses, making it an ideal solution for applications requiring efficient voltage step-up, especially when interfacing with low-voltage renewable energy sources like solar panels or fuel cells. Through comprehensive theoretical analysis and simulation, the proposed UDC performance has been validated. The results confirm that the proposed UDC outperforms traditional solutions in terms of extensive voltage conversion, making it a promising candidate for future energy systems.

articleTitle: Speed Control of Single Stage Solar PV Fed BLDC Motor-Driven Water Pumping
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a single-stage solar photovoltaic (PV)-fed brushless DC (BLDC) motor drive system optimized for water pumping applications using the incremental conductance (INC) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm. The proposed design eliminates the need for intermediate power conversion stages by directly coupling the PV array to the BLDC motor through a voltage source inverter (VSI). This integration reduces system complexity, cost, and power losses while ensuring efficient energy utilization. The INC MPPT algorithm dynamically tracks the maximum power point of the PV module under adapting irradiance and temperature conditions, enabling optimal energy extraction for sustained motor operation. The direct DC to AC conversion provided by the VSI enhances the system’s overall performance, driving the BLDC motor with high efficiency. This makes the system particularly suitable for water pumping applications, which demand robust, low-maintenance, and energy-efficient solutions in off-grid or rural areas. The system’s behaviour under dynamic conditions, such as fluctuating solar irradiance and partial shading, is thoroughly analyzed. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the single-stage design, demonstrating quick convergence to the maximum power point with minimal oscillations and consistent motor performance even in challenging environmental scenarios. This study underscores the potential of combining INC MPPT with a PV-fed BLDC motor drive, offering a sustainable, cost-effective and energy-efficient solution for renewable energy-based water pumping systems.

articleTitle: Innovative Eleven-Level Active Neutral Point Clamped (ANPC) Multi-Level Inverter for Enhanced High-Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A new boost ANPC (Active Neutral Point Clamped) inverter topology has emerged as a promising solution for applications requiring low DC-link voltage. The recently developed ANPC topologies have achieved a 2.5 -fold voltage boost. However, they generally demand a higher number of switches, adding to the system’s complexity. This paper introduces an enhanced boost ANPC topology that maintains the same 2.5 voltage gain while significantly minimizing the switch count. Additionally, the conducting switches are minimized, leading to enhanced system efficiency. The eleven-level (11L) output voltage is realized through switched capacitors, which feature naturallyvoltage balancing capabilities. The presented topology has been thoroughly analyzed, and its performance has collated with other ANPC topologies developed in recent years.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis of Nonisolated DC/DC Boost Converter for Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The implementation of renewable energy sources, including solar energy, is continually rising due to the depletion of fossil fuels and their harmful effects on the environment. Since the voltage level obtained from solar energy panels is low and varies according to the environmental conditions, it is necessary to use an DC/DC boost converter. In this paper, for photovoltaic systems a non-isolated DC/DC converter is proposed and the circuit dynamics are analyzed. The success of the proposed circuit is evaluated with the outcomes obtained from the study. As a result of the analysis with Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), the effect of different frequencies on the circuit operation is determined. With the recommended DC/DC boost converter, a wider range of output voltages is achieved compared to the traditional converter. It has also been demonstrated that the suggested strategy results in less output voltage fluctuation and overshoot. Additionally, the outcomes obtained from the FFT analysis can be used to evaluate the dynamics of the power electronic components in the circuit. On the other hand, compared to the traditional converter, it has been noted that the input current of the suggested circuit has higher harmonics.

articleTitle: Single-Phase Five-Level Common Ground Transformerless Switched Capacitor Inverters for PV Applications with Double Gain
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This article presents two new five-level transformerless common ground switched capacitor topologies with voltage boosting ability, self balancing of capacitors, and elimination of the leakage current for photovoltaic (PV) applications. They have reduced total standing voltage (TSV) in comparison with the recent typical five-level inverters. Both topologies uses one source, two capacitors, but topology- 1 uses seven switches and one diode meanwhile topology-2 uses six switches and two diodes. These topologies are built with minimum of the device count as compared to the various five-level inverters proposed in recent times and a detailed comparison among the topologies is presented to highlight the merits of the proposed topologies. A simple level shifted pulse width modulation scheme is used with proportional resonant ($\mathbf{P R}$) controller to validate the performance in MATLAB/Simulink software and their results are presented.

articleTitle: Integrated Filtering Solutions for Current Ripple in Single-Phase EV Chargers
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This study presents an innovative approach to integrating high- and low-frequency current ripple suppression techniques in a single-phase onboard charger for electric vehicles (EVs). As EV adoption accelerates, the demand for efficient and reliable charging systems has intensified, necessitating the reduction of current ripples that can negatively impact performance and component lifespan. We propose a combined methodology utilizing advanced passive filtering, active damping, and control algorithms to achieve significant reductions in both high-frequency (above 10 kHz) and low-frequency (below 1 kHz) ripple currents. Simulation results demonstrate a $\mathbf{9 0} \%$ reduction in high-frequency ripple and a 75% reduction in low-frequency ripple charging efficiency improved from $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$ to $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$, while thermal performance showed a notable decrease in operating temperatures, enhancing component longevity. This integrated approach not only simplifies the design by minimizing the number of filtering stages but also enhances user experience through quieter operation. The findings underscore the potential for optimized onboard charger designs that support the growing electric vehicle market while ensuring efficiency and reliability.

Author Keywords: Current Ripple Control Battery Management Systems

articleTitle: Backstepping-enabled Fixed-time Terminal Sliding Mode Control of Robot Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This work concentrates on the design of a backstepping global fixed-time resilient tracking controller for uncertain, nonlinear robot manipulators. Initially, to ramp up system dynamics and to increase disturbance rejection capability, terminal sliding mode control (TSMC) has been designed, which ensures finite-time state convergence to equilibrium. Later, backstepping-enabled TSMC has been developed to suppress the chattering and affirm global fixedtime stability. The qualitative analysis of the results demonstrates the practicability and excellence of the applied backstepping-enabled TSMC in terms of smooth control effort, quick convergence of tracking errors to equilibrium, and better shaping of transients. Rigorously, fixed-time stability of the closed-loop system has been demonstrated applying the Lyapunov theorem.

articleTitle: A Nine Level Switched Capacitor Multilevel Inverter with Soft Switching Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Switched capacitor (SC) based multilevel inverters (MLIs) find extensive applications across both low power and high power. Also, it is suitable for PV applications due to it’s common DC link and common ground features. Which makes it low-cost reliable efficient power converter for renewable sources. Switched capacitor have the self-voltage balance ability for capacitor which avoid auxiliary charging circuit and reduces the cost over conventional MLIs. In this article a new SC based nine-level MLI is presented for PV applications. The proposed nine level SC-MLI employs ten switches and a single switched capacitor unit to achieve nine distinct voltage states, resulting in twice the voltage gain compared to conventional configurations. The proposed inverter has common ground reduced number of switches, lower voltage stress, and inherent polarity reversal in the output voltage, all achieved without employing an H-bridge. The proposed topology is simulated and tested in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Theta-λ Optimization for Network Performance in Rician Fading and Multi-User Interference Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this paper, an investigation into the application of Theta- $\lambda$ optimization strategies to improve network performance is made in a challenging wireless communication systems environment subject both Rician fading and multi-user interference (MUI). This paper discusses the dynamic adjustments of Theta (angle-of-arrival) and $\lambda$ parameters necessary to balance system resiliency against high throughput. We did some simulations to test the performance in terms of latency, throughput as well as accuracy using values such frequency stability and jitter. The results show strong enhancements after the optimization - latency: from a mean of 20 ms to stabilizing at 15 ms, throughput: dramatically enhanced from existing baseline of around $\sim 50$ to 100 Mbps with enhancement between $\sim \mathbf{7 0 - 1 2 0 M b p s}$ while maintaining range and jitter reduction halved as average jitter is now less than two milliseconds compared previous Jitter at an optimal value. This had the added benefit of improvements in frequency stability: now, instead of hovering around 2.4 GHz like when we first tested it out-of-the-box, average was up to 2.5 GHz after optimization as well! The results of this study illustrate the potential for enhanced network reliability and availability through fading and interferer mitigation using Theta- $\lambda$ optimization. This case study is representative of the relevance for real-time adaptive optimization techniques in current-day telecommunications given surging demands on resilient wireless connectivity. Further research directions include enhancement of the optimization algorithms depending on specific network conditions and integration with adaptive strategies for real-time delivery using QoE-oriented mechanisms.

articleTitle: Adaptive Protection Scheme Using Optimal Coordination of Directional Overcurrent Relays in Grid-Connected Mode by Applying Micro-Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The integration of Distributed Generation (DG) in Grid-connected systems presents challenges in maintaining reliable protection schemes, particularly in coordinating Directional Overcurrent Relays (DOCR). This paper proposes an Adaptive Protection scheme that optimizes the coordination of DOCRs using a Micro-genetic Algorithm ($\mu \mathbf{G A}$). The proposed method enhances the resilience and adaptability of protection mechanisms against variable fault conditions and DG contributions. Through simulation studies, the performance of the $\mu$ GA-based approach is evaluated against traditional coordination methods, demonstrating improved fault detection and minimized relay operating times. Results indicate significant reductions in coordination time intervals, ensuring reliable operation of protection systems in the presence of DG. This research offers a framework for enhancing the operational reliability of power systems while accommodating the increasing prevalence of distributed energy resources.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Carrier Level Shift Pulse Width Modulation Using a Variable Amplitude Carrier Scheme for Multilevel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Reduced component Multilevel inverters (RCMLIs) are gaining popularity in industrial applications due to their enhanced output quality when compared to traditional inverters. A critical parameter for evaluating this output quality is Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). By selecting the appropriate pulse width modulation (PWM) techniques, it is possible to reduce THD effectively. High-frequency PWM schemes are particularly beneficial for switched capacitor MLIs, as they assist in managing capacitor inrush currents and enhancing capacitor lifespan. The newly proposed Variable Magnitude Multi-Carrier Level Shift PWM (PVMMCLSPWM) shows a notable decrease in THD compared to other high-frequency PWM methods available in the literature. Simulations of this technique have been conducted using a symmetrical nine-level MLI and benchmarked against the traditional Multi-Carrier Level Shift Phase Disposition PWM (MCLSPDPWM). The results of the comparative analysis highlight the enhanced performance of PVMMCLSPWM in minimizing THD.

articleTitle: Smart Home Automation with MQTT Using ESP32 and Node-RED
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to home automation utilizing the MQTT protocol. The system is implemented using an ESP32 node and a Node-RED server running on a Raspberry Pi, allowing users to control the system from the Raspberry Pi as well as client terminals. The proposed system enables users to control and monitor home appliances remotely from anywhere. By using the lightweight MQTT protocol, the system provides real-time communication between the node and the server and ensures responsive control and data monitoring. The implementation of the ESP32 node provides us flexibility and scalability, while Node-RED provides us with a user-friendly interface for system management. Experimental results validate the system’s effectiveness in maintaining reliable connectivity between node and server. This work highlights the potential of MQTT-based home automation systems to provide enhanced control and monitoring capabilities in modern smart homes.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electrical Infrastructure: The Benefits of Ultrasound Technology in Maintenance Practices
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Optimizing electrical infrastructure is crucial for ensuring reliability, safety, and cost-efficiency in the power industry. This paper explores the transformative benefits of integrating ultrasound technology into maintenance practices. Ultrasound technology, a non-invasive and non-destructive method, captures high-frequency sound waves to detect early signs of electrical failures such as arcing, corona discharge, and partial discharges. By providing real-time data on the health of components like transformers, circuit breakers, and switchgear, ultrasound technology enables predictive maintenance, significantly extending the lifespan of electrical assets. Traditional maintenance strategies often rely on time-based inspections, which can be inefficient and costly. Ultrasound technology offers a proactive solution by identifying defects such as corrosion, loose connections, and overheating at an early stage. This approach reduces downtime, enhances safety, and optimizes the lifecycle of electrical infrastructure. The paper delves into specific applications, including transformer inspection, switchgear evaluation, cable fault detection, and substation transmission appliance inspection, demonstrating how ultrasound technology is revolutionizing electrical asset management.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis of proposed 5 kWp Floating Solar Plant with Battery Energy Storage System at Ambazari Lake,Nagpur, India
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In the last decade, floating solar photovoltaic (FSPV) systems have opened up new avenues within the renewable energy landscape. By installing photovoltaic panels on water bodies, these systems take advantage of a cooling effect that reduces panel temperatures, thus improving their overall efficiency. Furthermore, FSPV installations are generally more economical compared to traditional ground-mounted solar photovoltaic (GSPV) systems. Unlike GSPV, FSPV offers numerous advantages, such as increased energy production, reduced water evaporation, minimal land use impact, and lower shading effects. This paper presents a techno-economic evaluation of the proposed 5 kW p FSPV system located at Ambazari Lake. Additional battery energy storage system (BESS) for floating solar PV (FSPV) plants is also proposed. A FSPV system with a BESS can improve the system performance by storing excess energy, responding to demand, improving power transmission, etc. Using PVsyst software and MATLAB code the technical and economic performance of the proposed 5 kWp FSPV plant was determined and compared with GSPV of the same rating. Ambazari lake is chosen as the location. The results show that FSPV produces 0.823 MWh while GSPV produces 0.772 MWh of energy annually. LCOE of FSPV is $3.080 \mathrm{Rs} / \mathrm{kWh}$ and payback of $\mathbf{1 0. 6}$ years. FSPV with BESS stores 15.5% more energy which is 1.131 MWh.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection using MobileNetV3: A Deep Learning Approach for Ultrasound Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this study a MobileNetV3 based deep learning model is developed for breast cancer detection on ultrasound images with the objective of reducing early diagnosis error and clinical decision making. The dataset comprises $\mathbf{1, 5 7 8}$ images categorized into three classes: Benign, normal and malignant. Data preprocessing steps (image resizing, augmentation (rotation, flipping, zooming), class weighting) were implemented in order to handle class imbalance and have efficient model training. The dataset was then split $\mathbf{8 0 \%}$ training, $\mathbf{2 0 \%}$ validation. With modifications such as extra layers to improve classification performance, MobileNetV3 was chosen due to its efficiency in handling large image datasets. Model was trained over 20 epochs with callbacks like Model-Checkpoint, ReduceLROnPlateau for learning and performance monitor. Overall the model achieves an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 2. 6 1 \%}$ with significant improvement on precision and recall for the NORMAL and Benign classes. Further areas for improvement were listed regarding the problematic misclassifications between Benign and Malignant categories. The results indicate a potential for clinical application of the model in differentiating benign from malignant cases, although better differentiation between benign and malignant cases requires optimization. Future work will consist of further improving generalization for more diverse datasets, and explore more advanced techniques, such as transfer learning and ensemble methods to improve performance in real world clinical settings.

articleTitle: Novel Voltage Sorting Technique for Uniform Load Power Distribution and Stiff Utilization of DC sources in Modular Reduced Switch Count Multilevel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Urge for efficient cost-effective power converter for active front end converters, Energy storage and Electric Vehicle (EV) applications has enhanced the significance of reduced switch count (RSC) inverter configurations with modular, redundant and fault tolerant abilities. However, to achieve the desired performance, a converter needs to be supported by a flexible voltage control algorithm with stiff utilization of DC voltage and uniform load power distribution ability. Among the conventional voltage control schemes, Voltage Sorting techniques reported for modular multilevel converters (MMC) are the most efficient in achieving stiff arm voltage balancing. Motivated by voltage sorting algorithms of MMCs, this paper proposes a comprehensive voltage sorting technique for modular RSC-MLI configurations to achieve uniform utilization of DC sources for both healthy and faulty (open circuit fault) operating conditions.

articleTitle: Bio-Inspired Adaptive Routing for Enhanced Data Transmission in Underwater Optical Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Underwater optical wireless networks encounter significant obstacles due to environmental factors like optical wave absorption and scattering that impact data transmission. To address these challenges, this paper presents an improved routing algorithm that incorporates Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) into a distance-adaptive dual-hop routing framework. By emulating ants’ natural foraging behavior, the proposed method enhances relay node selection, boosting both the efficiency and reliability of data transmission in underwater networks. The ACO-driven approach dynamically adapts routing decisions using pheromone trails and heuristic information, resulting in higher packet delivery rates and enhanced energy efficiency. Simulation results reveal that this optimized routing algorithm surpasses conventional methods, providing a resilient solution to the complexities of underwater optical communication.

articleTitle: Common Mode Voltage Mitigation using H12 Topology for Two Level Five Phase Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents the design, control, and analysis of common mode voltage (CMV) in five-phase inverters (FPI). The five-phase inverters provide smoother torque, better fault tolerance, and improved motor performance over three phase inverter topologies. However, common-mode voltage (CMV) transitions in the FPI are more complex due to the higher number of switching states, which can lead to electromagnetic interference (EMI) and leakage currents that shorten motor lifespan. To address these issues, a new inverter topology is proposed with two additional switches $(\mathbf{H}-12)$ in FPI is configured for DC decoupling. This approach effectively limits the transitions in CMV, which further reduces leakage currents, and minimizes EMI, overall enhancing system reliability and durability of drive system. The proposed $\mathbf{H - 1 2}$ configuration is analyzed and explained in details. The simulation is carried out using MATLAB/Simulink and results are verified for the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Strategic Deployment of Phasor Measurement Units in Power Networks Using Binary Brown-Bear Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A phasor measurement unit (PMU) is an instrument employed within the power network to assess real-time voltage and current phasors, leveraging a unified time source for synchronization. Their capacity to capture rapid fluctuations in frequency and the rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) is facilitated by their remarkably high sampling frequencies, typically ranging from 30 to 120 samples per second. The utilization of these metrics is essential for the oversight and regulation of the stability and reliability of the power network. Utilities can make the most of their investment in monitoring infrastructure by strategically placing PMUs. Utilities can attain optimal grid visibility and minimize deployment costs by determining the most crucial PMU locations by considering several aspects like network topology, load centers, system observability, redundancy, and generating sources. Therefore, choosing the strategic deployment of the PMU (SDP) is a crucial consideration. This paper employs the binary Brown-Bear optimization (BBOA) method on various IEEE test bus systems to determine the SDP. The focus of this analysis is on minimizing the quantity of PMUs while simultaneously achieving the maximum redundancy. The results derived from the presented BBOA technique are superior to those found in the existing literature.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Examination of Bipolar Coil with and without Ferrite Couplers
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Wireless charging has gained significant popularity due to its convenience in charging electronic devices without cables. However, aligning the receiver coil with the charging pad’s center is crucial for effective charging, which reduces the user convenience of wireless charging. This paper addresses this limitation and aims to improve the coupling of device placement by designing a dual D-coil (Bipolar) structure. It is observed that using a ferrite coupler and aluminum shielding improves the magnetic parameter as compared to the coupler and shielding. However, when the coils are misaligned, the efficiency improves, resulting in enhanced freedom of device placement. A dualcoil structure is proposed to improve power transfer efficiency compared to a single polarity coil. Simulation and measurement results confirm that the proposed coil design enhances the freedom of device placement while improving efficiency.

articleTitle: Eco-Connect: Examining Consumer Behavior and Sustainability in E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This research explores the intersection of trust, perceived risk, and sustainability in shaping consumer behavior when purchasing health products online. The study examines how e-commerce platforms can better cater to the growing demand for eco-friendly health products while addressing consumer concerns related to trust and risk. The findings indicate that trust remains a major determinant in consumers’ decisions to purchase health products online, with perceived risk, particularly in terms of product authenticity and online payment security, also playing a significant role. Furthermore, consumers are increasingly concerned about the sustainability of the products they buy, with eco-labels and clear information about eco-friendly products influencing purchasing decisions. The study highlights the need for e-commerce platforms to prioritize security, transparency, and eco-friendliness to attract and retain consumers.

articleTitle: Introducing a New Leg-Integrated Switched Capacitor Inverter Structure for Three-Phase Induction Motor Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)

authors.preferredName: K K N V A Manikanta

abstract: This paper introduces a new leg-integrated switched capacitor inverter (LISCI) structure for efficient three-phase induction motor operations powered by solar panels. Traditional inverter configurations often face challenges related to efficiency, size, and cost. The presented LISCI structure addresses these issues by integrating switched capacitor networks directly within the inverter legs, offering significant improvements in performance and compactness. Key features of the LISCI structure include reduced component count, enhanced voltage gain, and improved harmonic performance. The inverter’s innovative design enables it to achieve higher efficiency by minimizing switching losses and optimizing power distribution. Additionally, the integrated capacitors contribute to a more stable voltage output, critical for the reliable operation of three-phase induction motors.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis on Prediction Model of Hate Speech Detection Based on Social Media Data Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The exponential expansion of social media networking platforms has magnified the dissemination of hate speech, thereby requiring strong recognition systems to minimize its influence. The present work offers a comparative examination of many prediction models for the recognition of hate speech using social media data, employing Artificial Intelligence (AI) methodologies. The paper intends to assess the efficiency of several Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) algorithms for accurately detecting hate speech. The various strategies are evaluated using known datasets and measures including accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score. In addition, useful insights on the most effective methods for identifying hate speech are presented. The findings suggest that deep learning approaches are exceptionally effective at catching the contextual nuances of hate speech. AI-based hate speech detection apps improve accuracy and efficiency. Such systems are critical for creating a safer and more inclusive online.

articleTitle: An approach to Short-Term Load Forecasting by using AI based Model-Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Load estimation in advance is an essential aspect of load forecasting. As a developing country, India’s technological advancements and increasing daily activities lead to a rising demand for electricity. It is crucial for dispatch canters to maintain generation & demand balance, and forecast load in advance to ensure reliable operations. In the field of load forecasting, several AI-based models are available, but this work, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model has been chosen to forecast the load for Gujarat State. The model incorporates various input features such as historical load demand and calendar data, including previous week’s load demand, the day of the week, and weekend indicators. The analysis utilizes two years of historical data (2022 and 2023), focusing on patterns derived from load and calendar features. These selected features are used to train the ANN model, and the performance of model is demonstrated on test data for the year 2023, covering six months at various weekly intervals. Additionally, the training results and error metrics for six months of 2022 are also presented.

articleTitle: A Study of Power Electronic Converters for Wind Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The energy produced by wind and its benefits towards the surroundings have accounted wind energy to be a popular renewable energy source. To efficiently harness wind energy, power converters play a crucial role in converting variable wind power into stable electrical output suitable for grid integration or local use. This paper briefly summarizes the design considerations of various AC-DC-AC converter topologies for wind energy conversion systems (WECSs). This paper studies and compares various popular converter topologies intended for WECSs. A comparison table is included to summarize the merits and the demerits of the existing solutions for WECSs. The analysis demonstrates that the Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) topology offers significant benefits over other existing converters, making it a promising option for enhancing WECS. A component level MMC topology based closed loop system is simulated to verify its performance.

articleTitle: Impact of Data Preprocessing on Wind Forecasting Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: There is a high demand for renewable energy sources as non renewable energy sources are harmful to the environment due to its effects such as global warming. Among non renewable energy source, the wind energy is unpredictable in nature, making its integration with the grid a concern. By accurately forecasting wind energy, the stability of the grid can be ensured. The aforementioned can be achieved with the help of Machine Learning (ML) techniques. This paper investigate four ML techniques Multiple Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression, Random Forest Regression, and Decision Trees which are utilized and compared based on the metrics such as root mean square error, mean square error, mean absolute error, and R2 for three different cases. Initially errors are calculated without data preprocessing and later with data preprocessing. It is observed that preprocessing reduces error. This paper also investigates the effect of different seasons on the errors generated by these ML techniques. For this research, data is taken from National Solar Radiance database (NSRD) over two year period from January 2018 to December 2019.

articleTitle: Temporal Fusion Transformer -LSTM-based Improved State of Charge Estimation of Li-ion battery for Real Drive Cycle
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Precise measurement of State of Charge (SoC) in Liion battery is crucial for effective utilization of energy storage system. However, it is challenging with physics-based model due to computation complexity while data-driven model often lacks generalization for unseen data. To improve the robustness of data-driven model, hybrid algorithms are employed. This paper focuses on combining Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to improve the generalization of state-of charge estimation of unseen drive cycles. By leveraging the attention mechanism feature, temporal feature extraction of TFT along with memory capability of LSTM TFT-LSTM model is developed with optimal hyperparameters using Optuna framework. This model is used to estimate the SoC during the discharging cycle of a Turnigy Graphene Li-Ion Battery ($5000 \mathrm{mAh}, \mathbf{6 5 C}$) for the LA92 drive cycle at an ambient temperature of $40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Additionally, uncertainty analysis is performed against US06 drive cycle. Finally, the performance of TFT-LSTM is compared with LSTM model. The results demonstrate that TFT-LSTM achieves better performance compared to LSTM with Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of $\mathbf{1. 1 9 6 2}$ for unseen US06 drive cycle. These findings demonstrate the robustness of hybrid TFTLSTM against unseen drive cycle and highlight its potential under realistic conditions with variability.

articleTitle: Modeling, Analysis, and Prototyping of a Cascaded HBridge Multilevel Inverter System Using TI F28379D Microcontroller for High-Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: An investigation of the design, evaluation, and testing of a high-voltage-generating multilevel inverter system based on the TI F28379D microcontroller is detailed in this work. To evaluate the proposed system’s performance and feasibility, the research includes developing mathematical models, control algorithms, conducting simulation studies, and validating the results experimentally. We select a cascaded $\mathbf{H}$-bridge architecture for high-voltage generation to leverage the precise control and modulation capabilities of the TI F28379D microcontroller. We applied the CHB-MLI simulation model in MATLAB Simulink. Afterwards, the development of a 1 kVA prototype inverter at IPR confirmed the modeling results. Theoretical studies, simulation results, and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the designed multilevel inverter system, underscoring its potential for a wide range of industrial applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Cascaded FLC-FPID Based Maximum Power Point Tracking Technique For PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: For Photovoltaic (PV) systems to operate at the Maximum Power Point (MPP) and maximize energy generation, a control mechanism known as Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is required. There are many MPPT methods available. Because of their simplicity and cost efficiency, incremental conductance and perturb & observe methods are the most commonly utilized. But both the above-mentioned methods have common drawback that are fixed step-size and oscillations around MPP. To overcome this issue fuzzy logic controller (FLC) based MPPT is developed but it also suffers with steady-state oscillations around MPP. Hence in this paper, a new cascaded FLC-fractional proportional Integral derivative (FPID) controller based MPPT is proposed. In this, to study the performance of FLC-FPID a PV string with 4 S configuration is used. To test the proposed FLC-FPID MPPT a constant irradiance and variable irradiance conditions are used. The show the efficiency of proposed FLC-FPID approach is compared with FLC-PID and FLC. The proposed FLC-FPID approach outperforms the other two methods in terms tracking efficiency, oscillations at MPP, and tracking speed.

articleTitle: Non-isolated High-Gain DC-DC Converter with Moderate Gain for Hybrid Energy System Applications on DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A novel non-isolated High-Gain DC-DC Converter with Moderate Gain for Hybrid Energy System applications on DC Microgrids. The paper proposes a novel high-gain DC-DC converter for Hybrid energy systems such as Solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems, Fuel cells (FC), etc. The converter can replace the necessity of multiple converters for multiple sources. The major contributions are the lower switch voltage stress, High boost gain, multiple input capability, and lower component count as a dual source capability. The design and analysis of ideal and non-ideal conditions of the components are discussed and the individual effects of each component are analyzed. Further, the non-ideal gain and non-ideal efficiency are derived and presented. Also, Simulation results with a rated power of 100 W are presented.

articleTitle: A Frequency optimized architectural approach to lightweight authenticated encryption algorithm ACE-128
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Communication stands out as a vital function facili tated by the Internet of Things (IoT), making the secure transfer of data from origin to destination crucial. Traditional encryption methods can accomplish this task, but they often require a trade off between cost, security, and efficiency. In contrast, lightweight encryption provides an effective balance of robust security, affordability, and enhanced performance. Moreover, the reduced data volume involved in lightweight encryption decreases the chances of successfully breaching the cipher. The ACE cipher, a 128-bit lightweight authenticated encryption algorithm, employs a 320-bit(40-bytes) internal state and operates in a unified sponge duplex configuration. The architecture proposed has been tested and implemented across various FPGA families, showcasing an increase in operational frequency.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Three Phase Grid Integrated Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this presented paper a 250 KW three-phase grid integrated solar photo-voltaic system is modeled and simulated in MATLAB software. To extract the highest power from the sun, the P&O algorithm is utilized. For DC to AC alteration, a 3-level IGBT bridge DC to AC converter (inverter) is used with a PWM generator. Then the AC output power is finally injected into the grid. The system design and control scheme is accountable for the power flow between the DC source and the grid. To maintain synchronization between PV generator and grid, a VDC regulator, current regulator, and PWM generator is used in this MATLAB model. The simulation results are carried out at a given constant solar irradiance and also by implementing actual solar irradiance data of a day on the PV array. The manuscript is going to be addressed the simulation modeling and control of three-phase grid-integrated photo-voltaic system.

articleTitle: A Novel X-Type Six-Time Boost Switched Capacitor 13-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The demand for multilevel inverters is growing rapidly due to the increasing use of renewable energy applications. Traditional inverters are limited by high ripple current, voltage stress and switching losses underscoring the need for more advanced solutions. This paper presents a 13-Level inverter model using three switched capacitors, thirteen number of switches and two diode with six time boosting ability. The proposed circuit is designed for renewable energy applications, utilizing a single DC voltage source. The switched capacitors are self balance and does not require any auxiliary circuit for voltage balancing. Inverter performance is validated using MATLAB/simulink and PLECS software. Efficiency of the proposed inverter is found to be $\mathbf{9 8. 4 \%}$ and THD for output voltage and current were 8.68% and $\mathbf{4. 4 7 \%}$ at 1 kW load.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of High-Efficiency Three Level T - type Resonant Converter for the Charging of Electric Vehicle (EV) Battery
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The integration of a T-type inverter into an Inductor - Inductor - Capacitor (LLC) resonant DC-DC converter is motivated by its exceptional characteristics, including superior efficiency, minimal electromagnetic interference (EMI), and compact architecture, which are critical for addressing the growing demands of reliable and efficient electric vehicle (EV) charging systems. Conventional high-power charging solutions often face limitations such as excessive conduction losses, elevated voltage stress on components, and insufficient power density, restricting their adoption in next-generation EV technologies. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative Ttype LLC resonant DC-DC converter designed as a high-power charging solution for modern EVs. The converter incorporates a T-type inverter topology on the primary side and a full-bridge rectifier on the secondary side, achieving significant reductions in energy losses and enhanced operational efficiency. The design methodology emphasizes precise tuning of critical parameters, including the transformer turns ratio, resonant inductor, resonant capacitor, and magnetizing inductor, optimized for a power output of 5 kW and an operating voltage of 48 V. The system is modeled, developed, and validated through comprehensive simulations in MATLAB/Simulink, demonstrating notable advancements in reliability and efficiency. The proposed T-type LLC converter not only surpasses conventional solutions in performance but also provides a scalable and robust framework for high-power EV charging stations. With its high efficiency, reduced EMI, and compact design, this converter sets a new benchmark for sustainable and efficient EV charging technologies, driving innovation in future transportation systems

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Load forecasting involves estimating the optimal quantity of electrical power required for generation. It plays a crucial role for power companies in predicting the necessary power to maintain a balance between supply and load demand consistently. With the increasing trend of deregulation and enhanced competition in the global electric power sector, the importance of load forecasting has intensified. These forecasts are essential for facilitating energy transactions within competitive electricity markets. This study concentrates on short-term load forecasting through the use of the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) technique, which is a superior alternative to traditional methods due to its ability to manage variability and non-stationarity in load series. The framework is evaluated using a real-time dataset and compared against conventional Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The proposed LSTM model effectively tackles long-term dependency issues, such as vanishing and exploding gradients, demonstrating greater efficiency compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Detecting Butterfly species and finding the optimal classifier of the world’s rarest butterfly using AI image processing
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The main aim of this study is to evaluate the efficiency of different architectures of neural networks in classifying butterfly species, focusing on Palos Verdes blue, which is the rarest butterfly globally. We compared ten models using Leeds Butterfly Dataset including a Keras model built by ourselves, VGG16, VGG19 and several configurations of MobileNet with various levels of fine-tuning. The best performance was demonstrated by MobileNet with three layers that were fine-tuned. It had a test accuracy equal to $\mathbf{9 4 \%}$ and a loss at the order of magnitude 10. Furthermore, our findings show how model selection and tuning can be used to reduce computational costs while still maintaining impressive accuracy rates. This paper highlights why transfer learning and fine-tuning are important for precise identification of rare butterfly species that could serve as useful tools for ecological monitoring and conservation efforts. Additionally, this method can be applied across multiple biodiversity studies improving species identification accuracy in different ecological contexts.

articleTitle: Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model for Forecasting Electrical Load of Chhattisgarh State
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this paper, Electrical load forecasting for Chhattisgarh state has been accomplished using the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) model. The input dataset comprises electricity load data for the years 2021, 2022, and 2023. This data is utilized to predict the load values for the year 2024 and 2025. The Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) model stands as an exceptional forecasting tool, leveraging its instantaneous average-based architecture to predict future values with high accuracy. The model’s performance was evaluated using standard statistical metrics, ensuring accurate and reliable predictions.

articleTitle: Transition from AC to DC Residential Power Distribution: Deployment, Possibilities, and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The transition from Alternating Current (AC) to Direct Current (DC) residential power distribution is essential to align with India’s commitment for reducing carbon emission intensity by $\mathbf{4 5 \%}$ below 2005 levels by 2030 and achieving net-zero carbon emissions by $\mathbf{2 0 7 0}$. Out of total integration of renewable energy sources (RES), the solar photovoltaics (PV) which contributes around 57%, has enhanced interest in DC residential power distribution. The current technology in appliances, parts availability and its familiarity with customers, electricians, contractors and manufacturers have great advantage with ac grid supply. The shift to DC, offers numerous advantages, including enhanced energy efficiency, reduced conversion losses, and improved compatibility of RES with battery and DC-powered appliances. This paper reviews recent studies on the technical, economic, application and environmental feasibility of DC systems in residential buildings including the very nature of appliances. It also evaluates the challenges and possibilities of adopting DC-based residential systems, with a particular focus on deployment strategies, opportunities, and obstacles to accelerating the transition toward DC in homes.

articleTitle: Grid Integrated Solar Photovoltaic and Battery Storage System Interfaced EV Charging Station and Healthcare Centre Load
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents solar photovoltaic (PV) battery energy storage (BES) for fast DC electric vehicle charging station and remote healthcare center AC loads. This system is also interfaced with utility grid. A bidirectional converter is used to provide a connection between BES and EV systems via a DC link. EV uses a solar PV to consistently generate power throughout day. In lack of sunlight, EV depends on grid electricity. In grid synchronization control mode (SCM) and control of islanding mode (CIM) adaptable second order generalized integrator-based phase locked loop (A-SOGI-PLL) control method is employed for enhancing performance of system. Presented system is simulated in MATLAB/ Simulink environment under various weather and load conditions.

articleTitle: An Integrated EV Charging System with Solar Energy and LLC Converter Topology
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: By proposing a complete plan for Electric Vehicle (EV) battery charging systems, this research work advances the development of sustainable transportation infrastructure. For electric vehicles, integrating solar energy, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithms, with the LLC resonant converter (LLCRC) topology is a viable option to achieve high efficiency with less environmental impacts and better autonomy. The outcome of this study helps to create energetic and environmental-friendly transportation solution. The application of LLCRC in EV charger design is the main focus of the research. During the charging process, the LLCRC’s wide working range, high efficiency, and soft-switching properties are utilized to maximize power conversion and reduce energy losses. This strategy reduces the dependency on traditional grid supply and promotes an environmental friendly and sustainable transportation ecosystem.

articleTitle: Application of Spread-Spectrum Modulation in EV Battery Charging Systems for the Enhancement of Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Power electronic converters are primarily responsible for generating the necessary voltage in Electric Vehicle (EV) battery charging systems, which have gained significant attention due to their increased usage. Therefore, careful monitoring is necessary to ensure that the grid to which the EV battery charging system is attached improves its power quality. This work applies a simple and cost-effective Direct Sequence Spread-Spectrum modulation (DSSS) technique in the 3- $\phi$ AC-DC converter employed in an off-board EV charger to reduce the conducted Electro-Magnetic Interference (EMI). Upon implementing the proposed modulation technique in the converter, EMI is suppressed not only in the AC grid but also in the input side of the DC-DC converter that supplies the EV battery. The emission is reduced by 8 dBm and 38 dBm in the AC and DC current respectively in comparison with the Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation technique (SPWM). Moreover, the THD of the AC source current is reduced by 4.58% with a good improvement in the power factor. When it comes to improving the effectiveness and dependability of electric vehicle (EV) battery charging, DSSS modulation can be a useful technique which can increase the capacity by reducing interference and enabling more charging stations to run in a given region without significantly overlapping by dispersing the signal over a wider frequency band.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fault Detection in AC Microgrid Using Ensemble Learning Technique and Data-Driven Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Microgrids enhance power system resilience and renewable energy integration, but fault detection remains a challenge due to the complexity of their operations. This paper presents a fault detection model combining K-Means clustering with an ensemble classification approach utilizing K-Nearest Neighbours (K-NN) and Naive Bayes. The model effectively classifies fault types, including line-to-line, line-toground, and three-phase faults. To address data imbalance, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is employed, ensuring balanced fault detection. Evaluated on a simulated microgrid testbed, the ensemble approach outperforms traditional methods in both accuracy and fault identification precision. This study demonstrates the potential of integrating machine learning techniques into microgrid operations to enhance reliability, reduce downtime, and improve fault management in decentralized energy networks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Defense Against Cyberattacks in Power Grid Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper addresses the growing threat of cyberattacks on frequency regulation (FR) systems in modern power grids, which can destabilize operations through false data injection attacks (FDIA). To mitigate this risk, a cyber-physical model is developed, incorporating a 3DoF-TID-LADRC cascade controller optimized using QORSA, and tested on a modified IEEE 39-bus power system. The system integrates electric vehicles (EVs) and renewable energy sources like solar and wind. Additionally, an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy GAN (ANFGAN)-based detection mechanism is proposed to identify and counter FDIAs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively maintains system stability, keeping frequency and tie-line power deviations within safe limits, even under cyberattack scenarios. These findings highlight the model’s potential to enhance power system security and resilience.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of A Three-Port High Step-Down Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The rapid growth of multiport DC-DC converters in many applications leads to the reliability analysis of power electronic components used in the converter. Multiport converters are commonly utilized to manage power distribution among various power sources. However, a lack of detailed studies on the performance and durability under different operating conditions drives the need for the reliability analysis of multiport converters. This paper focuses on conducting a reliability analysis for a three-port high step-down DC-DC converter. The paper estimates the mean time between failures (MTBF) and overall system reliability. The reliability and MTBF are calculated by determining the failure rate of each component in the converter based on MIL-HDBK217 (Military Handbook). A complete reliability analysis for the three-port converter has been done in this paper.

articleTitle: Development of Ratio Water Index for Surface Water Mapping using Landsat 8 OLI Imagery
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Mapping surface water is vital for managing and preserving water resources. However, accurately identifying and measuring water bodies from satellite images is challenging due to similar spectral responses from various land types. Techniques such as spectral indices, Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning (DL) have been explored for water body identification. Implementation of ML and DL techniques requires labeled datasets and high computational resources. Spectral indices, in contrast, are straightforward, do not require labeled data, have better interpretability, and require less computational resources, but requires dynamic threshold determination. This paper proposes a Ratio Water Index, which eliminates the need of dynamic threshold and additionally compared with fourteen spectral indices formulated using Landsat 8 OLI images to determine the best index for extracting water bodies. Experimental results show that the proposed RWI outperforms by the performance metrics Overall Accuracy, F1Score, and Kappa Coefficient and recommended for efficient and accurate water body identification.

articleTitle: Solar-Powered VSI Speed Control of PMSM with Performance Analysis & Controller Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This study examines the integration of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) with renewable energy sources, focusing on solar photovoltaic (SPV) arrays to improve efficiency and sustainability in electric vehicle (EV) applications. PMSM, renowned for its high efficiency, silent operation, and precise control, is managed using a proportional-integral (PI) controller to handle variable load conditions, including fluctuations in torque and current. By fine-tuning the PI controller’s gains, the desired motor speed is achieved efficiently. A DC-DC Buck-Boost converter serves as an intermediary power conditioning unit, optimizing energy extraction from the SPV array and enhancing system efficiency. This setup ensures that PMSM meets the power and operational demands of EVs. Additionally, a voltage source inverter (VSI) facilitates electronic commutation of the PMSM, providing accurate control using fundamental frequency pulses. The system is modelled and simulated in MATLAB/Simulink, demonstrating its reliability under diverse load conditions. The findings underscore the potential of this approach in promoting renewable energy integration in EVs, paving the way for cleaner and more sustainable transportation solutions.

articleTitle: Novel Enhanced Astacus optimization algorithm for real power loss diminution in grid-connected renewable energy system
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Enhanced Astacus optimization (EAOA) algorithm is applied for solving the real power loss diminution problem in grid-connected renewable energy system. Astacus optimization algorithm is scientifically defined through the behaviour of Astacus. Astacus optimization algorithm initializes the population inside the search region limits by means of homogeneously distributed arbitrary quantities. Mutation factor and crossover rate are rationalized when the iteration count are reached predefined level. During this period temperature value and decreasing parameter are modernized. The value of the temperature will define the algorithm to perform the contention and searching periods or to execute the mutation factor and crossover rate. Procedure appraises fresh locations and appraises the entities when enhancements are found. Global best location and fitness values are modernized in all iterations and process end when best location identified. Horse racing betting strategy algorithm is based on the betting stratagem in horse racing. In the direct betting, gambler will bet on the particular horse and if the horse wins the race then the gambler gets complete reward. Astacus optimization algorithm is hybridized with Horse racing betting strategy algorithm to augment the exploitation ability. Enhanced Astacus optimization (EAOA) algorithm is validated in7 Benchmark functions, IEEE 30, 57, 118 bus systems and Grid 220 Kv system.

articleTitle: Super-resolution of Brain MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Image super-resolution (SR) has always been very important in the digital world. In the past year, a lot of work has been done ranging from frequency domain methods to spatial domain methods to reconstruction (LR) images. Deep learning (DL)-based SR technology is becoming increasingly popular in many fields, including medical imaging. High-resolution (HR) magnetic resonance imaging (MR) images provide more details for reliable diagnostic and quantitative imaging. HR brain MRI images are longer in duration and may cause discomfort to the patient, while LR MRI images are shorter in duration. To overcome this problem, we use a super-resolution convolutional neural network (SRCNN) to expand LR brain MRI images. We compare the results with the classical bicubic interpolation method. Comparative experiments show that the deep learning-based CNN method outperforms the state-of-the-art bicubic interpolation method.

articleTitle: A Simple Non-Isolated High Gain Three port DC-DC converter for Standalone PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) energy harvesting plays a vital role in promoting a sustainable and environmentally responsible energy future by offering benefits such as low cost, reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, and enhanced energy security. In this paper, a novel non-isolated high gain three-port converter (NHGTC) for SPV systems have been proposed. The proposed converter operates in five distinct modes: PV to both battery and DC bus, PV to DC bus, battery to DC bus, PV and battery to DC bus, and DC bus to battery. The key advantages of the proposed NHGTC include a reduced component count, high voltage gain, lower input current ripple and bi-directional current carrying capability at each port. Moreover, the proposed circuit offers a common ground connection to eliminate the issue of leakage current. All these features make the proposed NHGTC best suitable for the solar PV based power generation and energy storage applications. Validation of the proposed circuit has been carried in MATLAB Simulink under different modes of operation

articleTitle: Detection of Data Integrity Attack During Load Forecasting in Renewable Penetrated Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In a smart power architecture, the communication medium is a primary target for cyberattacks. When the network is exposed, the risk of intruding the system components to access, modify, or compromise sensitive information get increases. In smart grid (SG), the accurate load forecasting is crucial for achieving significant economic and reliability benefits within the energy market. Since the SG rely more on precise forecasting of electricity, their vulnerability to cybersecurity threats increases accordingly. However, cyberattacks targeting these forecasts can introduce wrong information, which can lead to incorrect operational decisions towards electricity delivery. This paper presents a statistical approach to detect data integrity attacks, thereby safeguarding the load forecasting process. Additionally, the forecasting model is engineered to recover the information very close to original information that was compromised with false values. The types of attacks considered in this context include ramp attacks, step attacks, scaling attacks, and random attacks.

articleTitle: Enhanced Normalized Proportionate LMS Control for Solar PV-based EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) depends on an infrastructure for charging that is both sustainable and efficient. This work provides a novel solution—a solar PV-based EV charging system controlled via an Enhanced Normalized proportionate Least Mean Square (ENP-LMS) adaptive control algorithm—to create a sustainable and effective EV charging infrastructure. With its quicker convergence, reduced error, and DC offset rejection, ENP-LMS outperforms the current approach in minimizing harmonic distortion, maintaining voltage stability, and facilitating optimal power extraction from solar panels, effective EV charging, and seamless grid integration. To achieve grid compliance, better power quality, and sustained and efficient EV charging, the suggested system, execution, and performance evaluation are all detailed in this work. The appropriate V2G and G2V procedures are verified by analysing simulation results under various transient considering grid-tied and standalone modes.

Author Keywords: Enhanced Normalized Proportionate Least Mean Square (ENP-LMS)

articleTitle: Design of Nine-Level Switched Capacitor-Based Inverter with Low Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This article proposes a nine-level (9L) quadratic boost (4B) switched capacitor (SC) based transformerless inverter topology for grid-connected solar photovoltaic systems. It uses a single source, 9 switches, 4 diodes, and 4 SCs. The maximum voltage across the SC is only half of the output voltage $v_{o} / 2$ and employs no complex algorithms for their voltage balancing. The power switches voltage stress is significantly low for the proposed topology and hence low total standing voltage per unit (TSV p.u.). Simulation and prototype outcomes are provided to demonstrate the viability of the proposed topology. The features of the proposed topology are shown through a detailed analysis comparing it with similar existing topologies.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Process Automation: A Case Study Using Q-Learning and Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
