abstract: Process automation is critical in modern industries, providing systems for precise control of variables such as temperature, pressure, and flow. Traditional control methods like PID controllers require manual tuning and often struggle with nonlinear dynamic systems. This paper presents a comparative study of two machine learning techniques namely Q -Learning and Decision Trees applied to industrial process control, specifically temperature regulation. Through a Python-based simulation, we evaluate the effectiveness of both techniques in real-time optimization. The results demonstrate that Q-Learning continuously adapts to system changes, optimizing control strategies, while Decision Trees provide reliable predictions based on historical data, reducing error margins. Our study shows that machine learning has the potential to revolutionize process automation by minimizing human intervention, enhancing efficiency, and improving system robustness.

articleTitle: Unified Kill Chain Model for Executing MITM Attacks in Microgrids with DERs
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The increasing integration of networked Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into microgrids is expanding the attack surface of modern power systems, particularly in decentralized environments. This paper explores the use of the Unified Kill Chain (UKC) framework to model and execute a Man-in-theMiddle (MITM) attack in a microgrid, focusing on the various stages of the attack, from reconnaissance to the final impact on the Microgrid Energy Management System (MEMS). By leveraging the UKC, the study demonstrates how sophisticated attackers can exploit vulnerabilities in communication protocols like Modbus to manipulate critical parameters, such as the battery state of charge (SoC), leading to erroneous decision-making and undermining the operational reliability of the microgrid. The paper underscores the need for targeted defensive actions at each stage of the attack chain to detect, mitigate, and neutralize the intent of advanced persistent threats (APTs) against DER systems.

articleTitle: Decentralized Robust Control of Uncertain SIDO DC-DC Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a decentralized robust voltage-mode control approach for an unstructured parametric uncertain model of a single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) switching step-down converter. Multivariable structure function (MSF) decouples the converter transfer function matrix into two individual channels. Then, the control strategy designs a decentralized controller for each channel. Finally, a decentralized control strategy is implemented on coupled SIMO switching step-down converter. Details of uncertainty modelling are discussed in the paper. To validate the approach, MATLAB simulation is conducted on the single-inductor dual-output (SIDO) buck converter system for robustness analysis using bounded uncertain frequency response plots. PSIM results demonstrate excellent steady-state performance under parameter variations. Experimental results are in close agreement with simulation results.

articleTitle: Development of a Power Controller for Simulating Decay Heat in Degraded Nuclear Core Materials
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A refractory ceramic lined core catcher is being developed at IGCAR for future sodium-cooled fast reactors. The lining is designed to safeguard the core catcher from high-temperature corium by limiting the downward heat flux. An experimental study has been planned to assess the adequacy of the refractory lining by subjecting it to time varying heat flux simulating radioactive decay heat during hypothetical melt relocation on the core catcher. The experimental setup consists of an electrically heated cavity, in which the ceramic specimen is immersed in a pool of molten tin to impart the heat flux across the thickness of the specimen. During the experiment the power of electrical heater should follow the decay heat curve which varies exponentially. Towards this, a power controller is designed using Arduino Mega microcontroller board interfacing ZMPT101 voltage transformer, ACS712 current transformer and Solid State Relay (SSR) to simulate decay heat flux for testing of materials under development of core catcher plate. A closed loop control methodology is adopted for efficient control of power. A test bench with a single phase resistive heater is designed to study the performance of P, PI, PD and PID controllers across various parameters such as RMS power, Settling time and Overshoot. The fuzzy-based PID controller effectively integrates the strengths of P, PI, PD, and PID controllers, significantly reducing peak overshoot and minimizing oscillations during steady-state operation while enhancing the accuracy of the average power output. Decay heat flux simulation is performed on an accelerated manner confirms the superiority of Fuzzy based PID Controller, achieving an average error of $\mathbf{0. 5 \%}$ by effectively employing different control mechanisms at various stages of power. Design, architecture, and testing details of the controller along with the performance assessment is outlined in the paper.

articleTitle: A Neural Network Based Framework for Load and Loss Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Neural Networks are widely used for prediction and forecasting in various fields and applications. The accuracy and non-linearity of artificial neural networks may vary according to the models used. Transmission line losses are inherent part of the system which may vary as per load variations. Here the proposed model ensures nearly accurate predictability of traditional line loss estimation that incorporates variation in active and reactive load demands. In this paper 57-bus system of sub-transmission network is used for test case where system losses are verified before and after training the data. The response was evaluated with change of total active and reactive power requirement.

Index Terms: Root Mean Square Error Of Cross-validation

articleTitle: Providing Security Solutions to IoT Devices Using Micro Version of Security Protocols over Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this research paper proposed micro version of Security protocol for IoT environment, it consist of three phases, in first phase all IoT devices must be registered with server to get user login credentials, in second phase the IoT devices which are really wants to access with server must be authenticated by server, and in third phase data is transferred through secure IoT channel by providing integrity, security and confidentiality. Data security is provided with twenty rounds of sub keys. In security context, to hide the probabilistic relation between transmitted data to cipher text we can use diffusion matrix. Diffusion matrix is used to protect from attacks and in our study we calculated diffusion matrix by varying p and q values. We observed that change of one bit in a single block may change many bits in cipher text.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Conventional and Modified Single-Phase Vienna Rectifiers for Power Supply Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Programmable power supplies usually comprise of a AC-DC front-end Power Factor Correction (PFC) stage followed by an isolated DC-DC converter stage. This PFC stage has to ascertain unity power factor at the input and provide a stable regulated DC voltage for the subsequent stage. Vienna type PFC rectifiers despite their complex control requirements, offer significant topological advantages. This work attempts to study and comparatively evaluate the single-phase Conventional Vienna Rectifier and the recently introduced single-phase Modified Vienna Rectifier. The suitability of these two rectifiers for a programmable power supply application is assessed in terms of the feasible operating range, topological requirements, input current THD etc. Simulation studies using MATLAB have been carried out to provide insights into the converter operation and performance.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Spectrum Sharing for Dynamic Resource Allocation in 6G Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: We conduct an extensive study on deep learningbased spectrum sharing to resolve dynamic resource allocation in 6G cognitive radio networks in this paper. The approach uses modern machine learning models to optimize spectrum usage, increase prediction accuracy of spectrum availability, and reduce interference among the primary and secondary users. We need to evaluate the performance of deep learning algorithms against the traditional spectrum allocation methods in simulation. In the paper, regular quality of service metrics such as throughput distribution and fairness among users are demonstrated to be much improved with these results, where both latency and energy consumption have been cut down dramatically. This work demonstrates the paradigm-shifting role of deep learning in spectrum management for $6 \mathbf{G}$ networks, pointing towards intelligent and effective resource allocation mechanisms in tomorrow’s communications.

articleTitle: Tunable Q-factor Wavelet Transform Based Features for Classification of Emotions Using EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Understanding human emotions is crucial for effective communication and interaction. Emotion recognition systems have gained considerable attention due to their potential applications in various fields, such as healthcare, human-computer interaction, and entertainment. Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising modality for emotion recognition, offering insights into the underlying neural processes associated with different emotional states. This study investigates the effectiveness of the tunable Q-factor wavelet transform (TQWT) for classifying different emotions using EEG signals. TQWT decomposes the EEG signal into subbands, and some features such as variance, skewness, kurtosis, and sample entropy are calculated from these subbands. These features serve as input to the support vector machine (SVM) classifier to classify emotions like happiness, fear, sadness, neutral, and relaxation. Experimental results of this proposed method demonstrate superior performance in classifying these five emotions compared to other existing methods.

articleTitle: Coordination Control of PSS and SVC for Dynamic Stability Improvement of Steam Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The steam power system is a crucial component of modern power system with high penetration of renewable resources. The dynamic stability of the steam power system is analyzed with classical model with positive synchronizing and damping torques of steam generator. The Simulink model is developed with all positive values of $K_{1}, K_{2}, K_{3}, K_{4}, K_{5}$ and $K_{6}$ and simulation is carried out for four cases. Case 1 is representing for Phillips Hefrron Model without any Controller, Case 2 is with Power System Stabilizer (PSS), case 3 is with Static Var Compensator (SVC). Case 4 is with coordination control of both PSS and SVC. The dynamic response of SMIB system is obtained for the load disturbance with step input for all four cases and obtained plots of angular frequency deviation and load angle or power angle deviations. The settling times of frequency deviation, load angle deviations for all four cases have been obtained and bar graphs have been presented in this paper. The coordination control of PSS and SVC enhanced the performance of steam plant with lowest settling time for both angular frequency and power angles, hence it has been observed that the dynamic stability has been improved significantly.

Author Keywords: Coordination control of PSS and SVC

articleTitle: Efficient Grid and Density based EGDBSCAN Clustering Method to Identify Global Noisy Points
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Clustering methods are used in many applications like psychology, computers, biology, and so on. DBSCAN is a one of the clustering algorithm which comes under density based clustering technique. DBSCAN algorithm clustering data samples based on density values, but all clustering techniques are proposed with various types of challenges. DBSCAN clustering method is also fail to detect all noisy points. In this research paper we a proposed a new novel efficient DBSCAN (EGDBSCAN) algorithm to cluster data set. First data samples are placed into grid cells, for each cell calculate LNPS, MLNPS, and NNPG values, all new data samples are added one by one to grid space and update the above mentioned parameters, and finally identify list of top ‘k’ global noisy points. Performance of proposed clustering is compared with KNN noisy detection method and we come to know that proposed algorithm shows better results.

articleTitle: A Brief Review on Protection Challenges, DCCB, Solutions and Advancement on DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A detailed comparison of various advance protection schemes adapted to provide reliable operation as well as secure performance in DC microgrids as compared to AC microgrids is provided in this paper. The integration of various generating units, loads (DC/AC), converters, and controlling units makes the system more complex and creates protection challenges. To obtain stable, secure, and reliable operation in DC microgrids, several advancements and implementation have been proposed by researchers and scientists in the field of solid-state devices. This paper discussed about various protection challenges, implementations of DC circuit breaker (DCCB) and solutions as well as future advancement of protection challenges.

articleTitle: Optimizing Plug-in Electric Vehicle Charging with Dyna-Q Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: To address the significant long-term charging costs associated with Plug-in Electric Vehicles (PEVs), this paper proposes a demand response (DR) strategy that considers various factors such as traffic conditions, fluctuating energy prices, energy consumption patterns, and the stochastic nature of driving behavior. Therefore, employing a Dyna-Q reinforcement learning approach in EV charging enables rapid learning and adaptation to other unknown parameters, such as energy prices and driving patterns Deep reinforcement learning techniques are utilized to address the problem, which is a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with uncertain transition probabilities. Unlike existing methods that either delay convergence or rely on user data, the Dyna-Q algorithm integrates both model-free and model-based learning, updating the model with each real encounter. A deep neural network-based value approximation method determines the longterm expected reward of state-action pairs because the state space is too big for a table-look-up method to work. Historical values are averaged to forecast future prices. Without the initial PEV owner data, simulations of three different user behaviors show that a Dyna Q network (DQN) method that does not use any models often leads to battery drain during trips. The results indicate that the recommended approach improves upon existing PEV charging techniques by more quickly and efficiently determining the optimal charging strategy.

articleTitle: Performance Validation of Wireless Power Transfer for UAVs Charging System Considering Misalignments
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Wired or contact power transfer (CPT) technology for electric vehicle (EVs) charging infrastructures has been commercialized by several manufacturers with either AC or DC charging configurations. AC charging system comes as Level-1 and Level-2 while DC charging system is either Level3 or Level-4. For DC charging systems which are known as fast chargers, shorter charging duration is the main advantage over the AC charging systems. However, both AC and DC based CPT require human interventions to plug the cable before charging process to take place. On the other hand, wireless power transfer (WPT) such as inductive, capacitive or laser beam based power transfer are the alternatives for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) autonomous charging techniques. Apart from being resilient to environmental factors like dust and water, WPT eliminates human intervention and the hassles related to battery swapping. However, WPT technologies have some limitations such as coil weight constraints and low charging performance due misalignment which hinders its efficient utilization in UAVs applications. Thus, this paper presents the performance analysis of WPT in terms of power transfer capability while uncovering several constraints for its deployment in UAV applications. Specifically, WPT performance parameters like power transfer efficiency, coefficient of coupling, and quality factors are analyzed in detail. The results of the analysis show that increasing the misalignment reduces the coefficient of coupling and hence overall power transfer efficiency.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Various SoC Estimation techniques for EV Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In present technological advances, the category of electric vehicles holds a prominent place. A reliable battery management system is required for an electric vehicle. Precise calculation of the State of Charge (SoC) in battery systems is important for effective energy conservation and extended battery life. This paper provides a thorough comparison of the many estimating techniques used to determine SoC. The techniques that are being examined include both established approaches like artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms like Feedforward neural network, as well as more recent approaches like voltage-based, Kalman filter techniques (Extended Kalman filter (EKF) and Unscented Kalman filter (UKF)), and Coulomb counting. Examined are the fundamentals, benefits, drawbacks, and suitability for various battery chemistries and operating environments of each approach. Through simulations and experimental validations, the evaluation process is carried out, offering insights into the precision, resilience, and computing complexity of each technique. The paper also addresses issues and potential paths for SoC estimation, highlighting the necessity of hybrid approaches that combine the best features of several techniques to produce improved performance.

articleTitle: Gesture-Controlled Robotic Arm for Real-Time Surgical Tool Assistance
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This research introduces a robotic manipulation system that leverages YOLOv5 for accurate surgical tool detection and Mediapipe for real-time hand gesture tracking to control a UFactory Lite 6 robotic arm. Designed for the surgical environment, this system enables intuitive, gesture-based control of instruments, minimizing manual interaction and maintaining sterility. Key contributions include a multithreaded, GPU-accelerated framework optimized for low latency, which achieves rapid response times essential for critical procedures. Results demonstrate the system’s effectiveness in reducing procedure time and cognitive load, significantly enhancing surgical workflow efficiency. Real world vigorous testing validates the design and methodology.

articleTitle: Dual Estimation of State of Charge and State of Health of a Battery: Leveraging Machine Learning and Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)

authors.preferredName: D S R S L Avanthika

abstract: Accurate estimation of battery state including state of charge (SoC) and state of health (SoH) are crucial for ensuring safety in energy storage applications. The SOC and SOH estimators were independently trained using the same input vector but with different objective functions, no integration between SOC and SOH estimations were explored. In this paper, a unified algorithm, for identifying both SoC and SoH states, is introduced by considering the Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter tuning. This approach allows seamless transition between SoC and SoH estimation without needing separate models for each task. In addition, equipping the dual estimation framework with a unified algorithm for identifying both states would impact the algorithm’s complexity. The suggested BiLSTM model reduces complexity in real-time Battery Management System (BMS) applications by eliminating the need for a separate model to estimate SoH. When compared to other machine learning and deep learning models such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Decision Trees (DT), Random Forest (RF), Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBF-NN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), and LSTM, the suggested BiLSTM method demonstrates the highest efficiency. Finally, to verify the proposed method’s effectiveness, a comparison among the different evaluation metrics was conducted. The proposed BiLSTM model achieved an average MAE (Mean Absolute Error) of 0.08 and NRMSE (Normalized Root Mean Squared Error) of 0.15 for SoC estimation across various temperatures $\left(5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, 15^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right.$, $35^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, and $45^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$), and an MAE of 3.12 and NRMSE of 0.23 for SoH estimation with a degradation rate of 47% of the cell estimated from the predicted capacity values.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic study of Rb2NaInI6 for solar cell efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this work, we utilize the TB-mBJ potential within the WIEN2k framework to investigate the properties of the material for its clean energy application of solar cells. The calculations reveal an indirect band gap of 1.719 eV. Additionally, the dielectric constant at zero frequency, $\varepsilon_{1}(0)$, is found to be 3.176. Thermoelectric properties were also calculated which demonstrated p-type optimal values. The material demonstrates strong absorption and reflectivity, indicating its potential for optoelectronic applications. The result analysis in this paper provides a broad understanding of the material’s behavior, highlighting its suitability for devices requiring efficient optical performance.

articleTitle: Automated Aeroponics System IoT-Based Monitoring and Control for Optimized Plant Growth
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Challenges of farming are getting worse due to pests, other environmental issues, and changes in the climate. Several novel technologies have been developed to improve plant growth and productivity, yet there are still numerous issues in this field. This suggests that daily improvements are needed. This paper provides an innovative automated system that uses a variety of environmental sensors, including as $\mathbf{p H}$, TDS, and humidity, for hydroponics and aeroponics. These sensors continuously monitor and modify crucial components to provide the perfect growth environment. In addition, the system has autonomous nutrient dosing, which reduces the need for human intervention and boosts overall effectiveness. Better control over the farming process is made possible by the system’s ability to scale and monitor in real-time thanks to the integration of IoT technologies. The study also looks at how machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) might improve crop health monitoring and growth forecasts. Additionally, an LED-lit indoor farming setup is included in the system.

articleTitle: Motion Detection Based IoT System for Optimizing Power Consumption
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) network to optimize power consumption in large halls, amphitheater, auditoriums, theatres, dining halls, etc., by controlling the appliances based on motion detection. The proposed network deploys individual sensor nodes at different zones with a microwave radar module for human presence detection and monitoring. The RCWL radar module, utilizing the Doppler effect and operating at $\mathbf{3. 1 8 \mathrm { GHz } \text {, is used to sense }}$ objects in confined aperture-based zones. After sensing human motion, the node utilizes the NodeMCU microcontroller board to switch the relay using an intelligent switching algorithm. Using the MQTT protocol, data is collected from each sensor node in the network and is shared and stored in a secure database. Node-RED dashboard is used to monitor and control the network remotely. An accuracy of nearly 95% is achieved after multiple iterations of prototyping and measurements using a 7.5-digit Keithley multimeter, RSA306B spectrum analyzer, and EMI and EMC probes.

articleTitle: Bi-LSTM based electrical load prediction model for a microgrid community area of Panama city
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)

authors.preferredName: D S R S L Avanthika

abstract: Accurate prediction of electricity consumption is essential for the efficient functioning of power grids and the successful administration of energy markets in the field of energy planning. There are several benefits such as system efficiency, dependability, safety, and stability with the proper forecasting of load demand. To ensure the proper operation of the microgrid energy management system, it is essential to predict the overall load demand with precision and consistency. A bidirectional long short-term memory network (Bi-LSTM) model is considered in this paper for the electrical load forecasting of microgrids. The proposed model is verified by using the standard available load forecasting data set of Panama City. Furthermore, the approach is compared with LSTM load forecasting method. The various performance metrics such as MAE, RAE, RSE, R2, RMSE, and NRMSE are employed in this paper to evaluate the accuracy of the proposed prediction model.. In this work, the Bi-LSTM method got the better error reduction values of $\mathbf{1 7. 8} \%$ in MAE, $\mathbf{1. 7 0 \%}$ in RMSE, 2.37% in NRMSE, 3.5% in RSE, 19% in RAE and 1.2% improvement in R2 when compared to the LSTM model. The proposed load prediction model is helpful in estimating the future power shortages of the microgrid community which leads to improve the system efficiency and reliability.

articleTitle: High frequency Area efficient architecture of lightweight authenticated encryption algorithm GIFT-COFB for resource-constrained IOT devices
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Safe and efficient cryptography solutions which may perform in the limitation of resources situations like Internet of Things systems etc is increasingly required, because the IoT continues to expand. These issues are resolved by lightweight cryptography, which minimizes memory and processing requirements while offering robust security. The necessity of cipher that strike an equilibrium between protection and sustainable use of resources is highlighted by the Internet of Thing’s explosive growth. Because of its resilience and effective design, the GIFTCOFB cipher stands out as a dependable choice. This work investigates the development of a high-frequency low area hardware architecture that speeds up the GIFT-COFB encryption in order to meet the performance needs of Internet of Things applications. Several FPGA boards have been used to model and implement the suggested high-frequency design, among them, the best results for maximum working freq, latency and area have been achieved in the seven series of Vertex and Kintex boards.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Dynamic Performance and stability of Autonomous Microgrid Utilizing Adaptive HBO-Power System Stabilizer
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Power and frequency instability pose significant challenges in microgrid operation, which restricts load sharing and degrades dynamic performance. Existing control methods often involve trade-offs between stability and power sharing. Conventional power system stabilizers (PSS) utilize lead-lag compensators with parameters selected arbitrarily, resulting in less than optimal performance during disturbances. This research paper presents a novel, generalized PSS designed for inverter-based microgrids. It incorporates an adaptive Honey Bee Optimization (HBO) algorithm for dynamic tuning of the lead compensator parameters $T_{1}, T_{2}$, and gain K. Unlike traditional methods, the proposed HBO-PSS improves the damping of low-frequency oscillations and enhances power sharing accuracy, while maintaining stable output voltage. The time-domain simulation results indicate that the adaptive HBO-PSS demonstrates superior performance compares to existing methodologies. The proposed PSS facilitates faster and more equitable power sharing, while also enhancing stability significantly, even in the presence of switching disturbances and higher droop coefficients. This work simplifies the implementation and analysis of PSS while facilitating future research into decentralized control strategies for distributed energy systems.

articleTitle: Customized Inverter Configuration for Multiple pole-Pair Stator Winding Induction Motor Drive with Reduced DC Bus Voltage
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)

authors.preferredName: K K N V A Manikanta

abstract: In this paper, A new customized multi-level inverter (MLI) configuration is proposed for induction motor drive, aiming to lower the requirement of DC bus voltage magnitude. This method utilizes pole pair winding coils separately to generate multi-level voltage waveform across the total stator phase windings. As the inverter requires lower input voltage it eliminates the requirement of boost converters when it is used in the EV applications. The inherent advantages of this topology significantly reduce control complexity in the battery systems by reducing the number of series-connected battery cells. The conventional LevelShifted Sine Triangle PWM technique proficiently shifts low-frequency harmonics to the carrier frequency, enhancing power quality and minimizing electromagnetic interference. Through MATLAB simulation, this new customized multi-level inverterfed open-end stator winding Induction motor is simulated and results are presented to validate the proposed concept. Ultimately, our research aims to contribute to advancing electric vehicle technology by operating the induction motor with minimal input DC source voltage, and substantial output gain.

articleTitle: Random Forest based Machine Learning Algorithm for Estimating State of Charge in Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)

authors.preferredName: D S R S L Avanthika

abstract: This paper proposes a Random Forest (RF) machine learning algorithm-based prediction model for the state of charge (SoC) level of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles. To show the effectiveness of the proposed prediction model performance, the RF model has been compared with the other machine learning algorithms such as Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Gradient Boosting (GB) approaches. The dataset includes cell temperature, state of charge (SoC), voltage, and current readings at three different external temperatures—15, 25, and 30 degrees Celsius are considered in this paper to test the performances of the proposed model. After preprocessing of the dataset, 20% of the data was used for testing and the remaining 80% for training purposes. The various metrics such as mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), coefficient of determination $\left(R^{2}\right)$, root mean squared error (RMSE), normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE), residual standard error (RSE), and relative absolute error (RAE) are usually preferred to evaluate the performance of the prediction models. The simulation results of the proposed model clearly show the effectiveness of SoClevel estimation for real-time battery management systems (BMS) when compared to other machine learning algorithms. The efficiency of the proposed model is $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$ and execution time is less than 5 seconds. The accurate estimation of the SOC of lithium-ion batteries is crucial for optimizing battery performance, ensuring safety, and extending battery life in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based DC to AC Dual Quasi Z-source Converter for Distribution Generation Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Using artificial neural networks to simulate a dual QZS converter high step up dc to ac converter is the main goal of this work. The standard converter of QZS with PI controller could be modified by incorporating an ANN controller, diode, inductor, and two capacitors to resemble the dual QZSconverter. The recommended dual QZS converter achieves all the benefits of a standard QZS converter, including continuous input current, voltage boost, and enhanced reliability. Furthermore, the recommended dual QZS converter reduces shoot through duty cycle by 30% without adding additional switches to the typical QZS converter, all at the same voltage boost factor. Acquired in both shoot through and non-shot through modes, simulation results are shown along with a description of the dual QZS converter.

articleTitle: Development and Performence Analysis of a tunable LED luminaire
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: At present the white Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) are mostly used light sources due to their extended lifespan, superior light output, and energy efficiency. This article presents an economical pulse-width modulation (PWM) dimming technique for LEDs to vary both the light output and the correlated color temperature (CCT) of the light source. The proposed approach provides a simple, stable, and inexpensive circuit design with adaptive PWM dimming method. A prototype luminaire consisting of two cool white and two warm white LED arrays has been developed and tested under low wattage conditions to verify the approach and its durability. This developed controller is compatible with the commercially available LED lamps and can function in various lighting scenarios. The study aims to demonstrate how the proposed PWM dimming technique can provide a tunable and dynamic LED luminaire. The relationship between the duty cycle and lighting parameters, including CCT, color rendering index (CRI), and illuminance are compared in this work.

articleTitle: Predictive PFM-based Digital Control Algorithm for LLC DC-DC Converter for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Conventional Digital Control of Power Converters, using the traditional Proportional-Integral(PI) regulators, has been a convenient and viable approach for practical implementations owing to their simplicity and less computation overhead. However, for higher-order systems, the frequency response of the plant model plays a vital role in determining the performance of the closed-loop system and the system requires multiple feedback loops for stabilization. Non-linear control approaches perform well in such cases. However, due to their complexity and the computation power demand, they are reluctantly looked upon, if ever, especially in automotive applications. In this paper, an optimized Predictive PFM(Pulse Frequency Modulation)-based digital control algorithm is presented which works well for systems with inferior frequency-domain parameters, adeptly uses the computation power, can smoothly mitigate disturbances for accurate control of the LLC DC-DC Converters and does not require tuning for use in different systems.

articleTitle: Cyber Attack Detection using Stacking Ensemble Model for Internet of Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The Internet of Vehicle (IoV) is an advancement in transportation by integrating vehicles to each other, road-side infrastructure, and smart control units. However, this interconnection of the IoV system, introduces different kinds of cyber security challenges such as data privacy, integrity, denial of services and unauthorized access attacks. The traditional methods of attack detection face various challenges in addressing sophisticated attacks due to limited scalability and inability to handle large complex dataset. Thus, this paper introduces a model for detecting cyber-attacks within IoV system using a stacking ensemble technique. In the proposed stacking method, four base classifiers such as Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, and Decision Tree as a Meta classifier are used to identify cyber attacks effectively. The CICIoV-2024 dataset is used to evaluate the performance of the proposed model and it is observed that the proposed model performs better with 97% accuracy, 94.24% precision, 99.24% recall, and 96.68% F1-score as compared with state-of-art models.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Grid-Tied Solar PV System using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This work presents a compact design for a grid-tied solar energy system that integrates both conventional closed-loop (CL) control and machine learning (ML), offering a comparative analysis of their performance. The efficiency of a solar panel is influenced by several key factors, including temperature, irradiance, voltage, and current. Sudden variations in these parameters can affect the grid current, which in turn affects the power output. The primary objective is to evaluate the efficient operation of ML in this context. The study highlights that during sudden changes in temperature and irradiance, the output voltages of the photovoltaic (PV) array and the boost converter are more stable and accurate with ML-based control. The Levenberg-Marquardt ML algorithm performs superior to the classical Bayesian algorithm under these conditions, delivering well-regulated voltage and current at the output of the boost converter and inverter, respectively. Furthermore, the regression for testing and validation achieves a high accuracy of up to 0.9, demonstrating the effectiveness of the ML approach.

articleTitle: Advanced Temperature Forecasting in Major Indian Cities: A Comparative Study of SARIMA, Prophet, and XGBoost Models
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of temperature forecasting models across major Indian cities: Mumbai, Kolkata, Delhi, and Chennai by three methodologies that are Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), Prophet, and XGBoost. By analyzing historical temperature data, we implement a methodology that includes data collection, preprocessing, model selection, training, and evaluation. To evaluate the stationarity of the dataset, the Augmented Dickey-Fuller test is used, and seasonal differencing is applied to achieve stationarity. Both seasonal and non-seasonal components are fitted in the SARIMA model. The Prophet model is also fitted in handling missing data and trends, and XGBoost through machine learning techniques. The performance of each of the three models is evaluated by Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). The forecasts are generated for six years and this study contributes to climate science by a comprehensive evaluation of temperature forecasting methodologies, that could be helpful in urban planning and policy-making.

articleTitle: A Prototype of an Intelligent Door Lock Device with Hybrid Security Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The traditional smart locks available on the market are externally accessible, single-stage devices that pose potential risks of physical damage and hacking, primarily due to their visibility to the outside. To mitigate these challenges, we propose a prototype for a two-stage door lock system, comprising a Primary Lock followed by a Main Lock, integrating a hybrid smart security verification process. This model utilizes RFID and Bluetooth HC05 modules for authentication at the Primary Stage Security System (PSSS), which governs access to the Primary Door (external). Additionally, it implements a fingerprint scanner and voice recognition modules for authorization at the Secondary Stage Security System (SSSS), which controls access to the Main Door (internal). The requirement for mandatory user credential verification at both access stages enhances the security and robustness of this smart lock system.

articleTitle: Mutual Inductance Estimation for Series-Parallel Compensation Topology in Drone’s Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A major technical limitation in wireless power transfer (WPT) systems for drones is power transfer coil misalignment, which causes fluctuation in the coupling coefficient between coils that impacts the system’s efficiency. This paper proposes a unique method to mitigate the effect of variation in the coupling coefficient by regulating the inverter’s phase shift, based on the estimated mutual inductance and load current value, these estimations use the primary side measurements only. The developed mathematical model and simulation findings indicate the proposed primary side constant current control technique improves the system’s efficiency without relying on secondary side feedback, eliminating the wireless communication devices on the receiver side, which enhances the drone’s payload capacity by reducing onboard weight. This proposed topology stabilizes the performance even in misalignment and fluctuation in the coupling coefficient, improves flight endurance, reduces complexity, and ensures reliable operation in dynamic real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: THD reduction with 5-level inverter using SPWM Technique for Solar Array connected to Load
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The hybrid microgrid (MG) has become more and more popular lately since it combines the advantages of renewable power sources. Since MG has more than single subgrids, connecting converters is required. Since non-linear AC loads degrade the quality of the supply voltage on the AC bus, it is promising to add an additionalharmonic correction mechanism to the interlinking converters. Since the primary aim of interlinking converters is to exchange actual and reactive power between the grids, the standard harmonic regulating strategy used for active power filters (APFs) may not be suitable for them. It is preferable for the switching frequency to be lower than the APFs when the MG’s capacity is high. One option that offers several advantages for usage of hybrid microgrid energy resource is photovoltaic (PV) energy generating. A PV with multilevel inverter (MLI) connected to load is studied in this research. By generating the AC output terminal voltagefrom multiple voltage levels, the MLI providesa few benefits, including higher power quality, lower total harmonic distortion THD content in sinusoidal current waveforms, and less strain on the switching components. This meets the load’s connection requirements and offers increased power conversion efficiency. However, to improve system performance, a maximum power point tracker (MPPT) is crucial in suchlike system. To guarantee a quick dynamic reaction, a control algorithm based on maximum power point tracker has been devised for the 3-level 3-phase inverter and five level three phase inverters in this study. Simulation of the suggested system model was done in MATLAB/SIMULINK. Additionally, test results are shown to confirm that the suggested strategy is feasible.

articleTitle: Optimizing Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment Pipelines for Enhanced Interactive Streaming Experiences
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Seamless user experiences in this ever-evolving domain of interactive streaming applications need to be qualitative in nature. This paper deals with the design of Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment pipelines in relation to the specialty of interactive streaming applications for their implementation and optimization. For addressing problems regarding real-time content delivery, interactivity by users, and scalability of the system, the modern practices of continuous integration/continuous deployment have been applied here. Our approach integrates automated testing, continuous monitoring, and iterative deployment strategies for robust performance, fast bug resolution, and dynamic feature updates. We provide case studies illustrating how CI/CD has reduced downtime, increased user engagement, and hastened time-to-market. Based on the findings, an optimized CI/CD pipeline not only streamlines development processes but also greatly contributes to overall improvement in the interactive streaming experience. Index Terms—Continuous Integration, Continuous Deployment, Interactive Streaming, Automated Testing, Real-Time Content Delivery, System Scalability, User Engagement, Development Pipeline Optimization

articleTitle: Automated Cardiomegaly Detection from Chest X-rays Using InceptionV3: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this work, InceptionV3 is applied to identify cardiomegaly from chest X -ray images through a deep learning technique. The dataset, sourced from Kaggle, contains 5,552 balanced images across two classes: The presence of cardiomegaly, coded as “True” and the absence of cardiomegaly coded as “False”. Some pre-processing steps which include image resizing, normalization and augmentation improved the performance of the proposed model. The model was trained in 10 epochs with a batch size of 64 and produced an overall accuracy of 86%. The evaluation criteria such as precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix and classification report proved high and fair results on both classes. The results show a slight overfitting problem, which needs to be address in the future work by using approaches such as regularization and dropout. Future work includes using real and bigger datasets, combining different types of data, and using eXplainable AI for increased model interpretability. This work establishes the possibility of using deep learning for automating the identification of cardiomegaly, which can be an important direction for the development of efficient and accurate diagnostic tools in medical imaging.

articleTitle: A Robust Controller of a New Transformer-Less Quasi-Switched Converter with Low Current Ripples for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This article presents a novel transformer-less modified structure of a quasi-switched non-isolated converter applicable for auxiliary loads in electric vehicles. The primary feature of this quasi-arrangement is providing continuous load current with low-order ripples operating at a nominal duty cycle range. In comparison to existing configurations, the proposed topology achieves higher efficiency, a better voltage conversion ratio, and alleviates voltage, and current stresses across the power switch. Furthermore, the converter is designed with fewer components and optimized with a robust controller, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) is incorporated to achieve better output response, reduced peak overshoot at 0.3%, and faster settling time. Overall, the system achieves a peak efficiency of approximately $\mathbf{9 6. 2 \%}$. The operating principle, theoretical, steady state analysis, and comparison with existing topologies have also been incorporated. To validate the system’s performance, a 200 W hardware prototype will be built, developed, and tested to verify the experimental results.

articleTitle: A novel fault detection scheme based on a cumulative sum of superimposed positive sequenceenergy for microgrid protection
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Incorporating distributed generations (DGs) into microgrids requires an effective fault detection mechanism. However, conventional approaches have limitations in achieving reliable and accurate outcomes under complex and abnormal conditions in microgrid distribution systems. Recent studies have demonstrated superimposed sequence components’ effectiveness in fault detection and location. This study proposed a novel fault detection method based on the cumulative sum of superimposed energy (CUSUM-SE), considering positive sequence components. The efficiency of the proposed method is evaluated under a wide range of symmetrical and unsymmetrical fault scenarios, including fault occurrences at different locations. The proposed methodology is further tested for robustness in detecting simultaneous and high-resistance faults (HRFs). The effect of DG penetration on the protection scheme is also analyzed. The proposed approach is validated on the Consortium for Electric Reliability Technology Solutions (CERTS) AC microgrid using the 2021a MATLAB/Simulink platform, demonstrating its consistency and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of 3D PCB Rogowski Coil in Pulsed Current Measurement Using Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper explores using a Printed Circuit Board Rogowski coil (PCB RC) as a sensor for measuring pulsed current (PC) signals. A key aspect in developing the PCB RC prototype is carefully selecting the terminating resistance, which is vital for accurately calibrating the sensor’s response to PC signals. The impact of the terminating resistance on the performance of the PCB RC is evaluated through Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations. The 3D design and modeling of the PCB RC for pulsed signal measurement are performed using Ansys Maxwell. The electrical parameters obtained from simulations closely match the analytical values. Furthermore, the frequency response of the PCB RC is analyzed under different terminal resistances. The 3-D PCB RC model is tested with a 200 mA (peak) pulsed current signal under various terminal resistances. The output voltage of the PCB RC is estimated and analyzed using FEM methods. Additionally, the sensitivity of the PCB RC is calculated.

articleTitle: A Multilevel Inverter with Streamlined Components and Reduced THD using the Multicarrier Sine PWM Approach for Resistive and Inductive Loads
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In the intriguing realm of power electronics, this paper examines the design process of a revolutionary 129-level inverter, where creativity and imagination meet. This inverter, which embraces the inscrutability of having fewer components and goes beyond harmonic norms, is a paradigm shift in multilevel converter technology. The journey starts with an innovative method that intentionally reduces parts and toggles, challenging the common statement that higher levels require more complexity. As a result, a fascinating symphony of voltage steps smartly rises to $\mathbf{1 2 9}$ levels while simultaneously lowering the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). The waveform of the inverter mimics a sine wave with unparalleled fidelity, akin to a mystical incantation. A careful control strategy that smoothly switches by Multicarrier Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (MSPWM) technology underpins this amazing performance. In addition to reducing THD, the control mechanism fully utilizes the inverter’s fewer components. This paper reveals not just an inverter but also an enchanted object that surpasses traditional bounds as it invites readers to explore the imaginary world of power electronics. This $129-l e v e l ~ m a r v e l ~ i n v i t e s ~ s c i e n t i s t s, ~$ engineers, and dreamers to set out on an exploration, widening the boundaries of what is imaginable in the magical field of power conversion.

articleTitle: Blockchain for Secure and Decentralized Power System Operation in Smart Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The incorporation of blockchain technology into smart grid operations has attracted considerable attention owing to its decentralized, immutable, and transparent characteristics. This study examines the use of blockchain in the IEEE 14 bus system, illustrating its capacity to improve security, transparency, and resistance against cyber threats. The suggested system utilizes blockchain to guarantee safe data flow among nodes, including power generators, loads, and control centers. Every transaction related to power flow data, control signals, or market operations is recorded on an immutable ledger. The decentralized architecture of blockchain allows nodes to independently validate transactions through consensus processes such as Proof of Work (PoW) or Proof of Stake (PoS). This decentralization removes a singular point of failure, hence diminishing susceptibility to cyber-attacks aimed against centralized systems. Data integrity is safeguarded using cryptographic hash functions, which promptly identify any attempts to modify the stored information. The blockchain consensus system guarantees the recording of only valid transactions, hence enhancing security. Mathematical models for power flow analysis are incorporated into the blockchain framework, guaranteeing precise computations of voltage magnitudes, phase angles, and power transfers among buses. Simulations of the IEEE 14 bus system demonstrate enhanced system security and resilience, particularly against False Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs). The findings underscore how blockchain enhances overall reliability and mitigates the danger of unwanted data alteration. Blockchain enhances transparency and decentralization, providing a promising approach for guaranteeing the future of smart grid operations.

articleTitle: A Bidirectional-LSTM-Based Fractional Power System Stabilizer for Effective Power Oscillation Damping
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Power oscillations in modern electrical grids are increasingly prevalent and threaten system reliability. Addressing this issue necessitates implementing robust damping methods to ensure system stability. This paper presents a novel approach to designing a Fractional Power System Stabilizer (FPSS) to effectively mitigate power system oscillations. The FPSS parameters are forecasted using a Bidirectional Long-Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network, trained through phase compensation techniques. The proposed Bi-LSTM-based FPSS offers enhanced predictive accuracy for parameter tuning, thereby improving damping performance. Comprehensive simulations under various operating conditions and test scenarios demonstrate the FPSS’s superior effectiveness in maintaining system stability compared to traditional stabilizers. The results highlight the potential of the Bi-LSTM-based FPSS to improve the reliability and robustness of modern power systems.

articleTitle: Two stage grid-connected T-type APF with improved power quality
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This study presents grid-connected two-stage active power filter using three-level T-type multilevel inverter ($\mathrm{T}^{2} \mathrm{MLI}$) and a DC-DC boost converter. The $\mathrm{T}^{2} \mathrm{MLI}$ integrate benefits of a three-level inverter with the advantages of a twolevel inverter, such as reduced switching loss, fewer switching components, and simplified control techniques. The APF control scheme is designed using least mean square algorithm, which estimates the reference current online to ensure compensation performance. The DC-DC boost converter, connected on the DC side of the APF, utilizes the perturb and observe (P&O) method-based maximum point tracking algorithm to optimize power extraction from PV source. The simulation results of the two-stage APF is presented using MATLAB/Simulink platform, showing the efficacy of the proposed two-stage APF in facilitating solar power integration into grid.

articleTitle: Efficiency Enhancement of Perovskite Photovoltaic Cells by Incorporation of NiO2 HTL
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In order to achieve high hole capturing rates and minimal minority carrier loss in PV cells, the hole transport layer (HTL) materials in Copper Zinc Tin Sulfide (CZTS) photovoltaic cells (PCs) are essential. Up to this point, CZTS cells based on HTL materials with high minority carrier loss minimization have only been developed. In order to create an effective CZTS PV cell, numerous researchers are looking into wide energy bandgap HTL materials. This paper proposes a novel wide bandgap NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as a HTL nanomaterial for a highefficiency photovoltaic cell. Additional analysis, energy band alignment matching, layer thickness and doping density optimization, and base-based proposed PV cell construction. The CZTS/NiO $\mathbf{N}_{2}$ based PV cell performs better, with $\mathrm{Voc}=1127$ $\mathrm{mV}, \quad \mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{sc}}=28.17, \quad \mathrm{FF}=\mathbf{8 4. 2 6 \%}, \quad$ efficiency $=26.74 \%$, and EQE $=82 \%$.

articleTitle: Improving Faster R-CNN for Vehicle Detection under Varying Conditions with Domain Adaptation Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid progress in autonomous driving technology has transformed the automotive industry, positioning vehicle detection as a vital component to guarantee secure and efficient navigation. This article presents an upgraded Faster R-CNN architecture that incorporates a SelfSupervised Thermal Network (SSTN) to advance vehicle detection, specifically in unfavorable weather conditions. This model is built using MobileNetV3 as its backbone and is enhanced with a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) for extracting features at multiple scales. Additionally, it employs self-training and pseudo-labeling techniques to facilitate domain adaptation. The model is trained and tested using the DAWN dataset, which includes difficult scenarios such as fog, rain, sandstorms, and snowstorms. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved Faster R-CNN with SSTN significantly outperforms some modern methods, achieving an accuracy of 87.15%, a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 85.20%, and a recall rate of 81.37%. Although it lacks behind the traditional method like HOG-SVM. This approach enhances the reliability of vehicle detection systems in varying environmental conditions, making it a valuable contribution to the development of robust autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cardiac Diagnosis: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Techniques for ECG Signal Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Myocardial Infarction (MI), commonly known as a heart attack, arises from the interruption of blood flow to the heart muscle, causing tissue damage and necessitating prompt and accurate diagnosis for effective treatment. Electrocardiograms (ECGs) are a crucial diagnostic tool for MI due to their non-invasive nature and real-time monitoring capabilities, although their utility can be compromised by noise, signal variations, and complex waveforms. In this study, we address these challenges by performing a comparative analysis of various machine learning (ML) algorithms to enhance MI detection from ECG signals. We categorized ECG data into five distinct classes: Normal, Fusion of Paced and Normal, Premature Ventricular Contraction, Atrial Premature, and Fusion of Ventricular and Normal. Our goal was to determine which ML models achieve the highest accuracy in classifying these classes and thus improving diagnostic precision. We evaluated seven ML algorithms—AdaBoost, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machines, K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forests, and XGBoost. Among these, XGBoost demonstrated the highest accuracy of $\mathbf{9 7 \%}$, highlighting its effectiveness in MI detection from ECG data.

articleTitle: Dead-Time Compensation for VSI-fed Induction Motor System Considering Snubber and Parasitic Capacitance and Resistance
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: During the modulation process of the voltage source inverter-fed motor drive system, to prevent the short circuit fault, the dead-time is introduced, resulting in nonlinear voltage errors, low-order harmonic distortion and torque ripple. To improve the effect of dead-time compensation, considering snubber and parasitic capacitance and resistance parallel connected with the switching tube, the equivalent circuit during the dead-time is established, and the state equation of the parasitic capacitor voltage is derived. Then, the voltage error expression with the time is obtained. After online compensation, the voltage error and the current harmonics are reduced. Finally, the simulation and experiment are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed dead-time compensation scheme by considering the snubber and parasitic capacitance and resistance.

articleTitle: Linear Discriminant Analysis based Scheme for Fault Detection and Classification of Internal and External Faults in Hybrid Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Hybrid AC-DC transmission lines are used to increase the transmission capacity and reliability with the integration of renewable energy. However, the occurrence of faults in these transmission systems has been a major concern in its operation. The paper proposes a method for detecting faults along with identification of internal and external faults in hybrid overhead transmission lines. The method is based on a linear discriminant analysis machine learning model. A hybrid AC-HVDC transmission line is simulated for obtaining training and testing data which contains no fault and fault data at different fault scenarios. A discrete Fourier transform is applied as feature extraction technique to obtain the fundamental current and voltage profiles during various types of AC and DC faults at several locations on the transmission line. The effectiveness of the proposed method in precisely detecting and identifying internal and external faults is confirmed by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Integrated Design of MPPT and DC-DC Buck Converter for Efficient Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The increasing threats of global warming and the urgent need to transition to renewable energy systems have amplified the demand for efficient and sustainable battery charging solutions. This paper presents a novel integration of a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm that utilises a modified Perturb and Observe (P&O) method based on Proportional Integral (PI) control and an enhanced battery charging algorithm for a $24 \mathrm{~V}, 100 \mathrm{Ah}$ lead-acid battery. The research implements the proposed control system through a buck converter functioning as a charge controller. The algorithm dynamically regulates the duty cycle of the DC-DC converter’s switch through the implementation of the Perturb and Observe (P&O) MPPT technique to maximize power extraction. It offers precise management of the battery charging voltage and current across various charging phases. This approach ensures battery safety by preventing overvoltage and overcurrent while also extending the lifespan by optimizing the charging rate. The entire system is implemented and tested in the MATLAB/Simulink environment, validating the robustness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Single Phase Transformerless Grid Connected PV Inverter Configurations: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Power inverters play a crucial role in photovoltaic system (PVs) applications. Transformer less inverters pose several advantages over transformer-based PV inverters, including decreased size, minimal cost, and better efficiency by eliminating the need for a transformer. However, a major drawback is the leakage current which is caused due to the absence of galvanic isolation between the PV panels and grid. This research presents performance analysis of $\mathrm{H} 4, \mathrm{H} 5, \mathrm{H} 6$ and Improved H6 inverters simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK software to minimize the leakage current.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Classification of EEG subjects using Hybrid Machine Learning algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Recurrent Epileptic seizures are neurological events described by irregular electrical activity in brain, detectable through electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Accurate detection of seizures is crucial for timely medical intervention by effective management and treatment. This paper presents end-to-end approaches to detect seizures from EEG subjects using K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT) and a proposed Hybrid ML model. BONN Dataset is used to collect EEG subjects in this study. Our developed KNN, SVM and DT algorithm attained an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4 \%} \% \mathbf{9 6. 6 7 \%}$ and $\mathbf{9 6. 6 6 \%}$. The developed hybrid algorithm improved the performance and accomplished an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 7. 3 3 \%}$. The developed end-to end models are very robust, effective and helps in automated seizure detection.

articleTitle: Optimized Adaptive Technique For Denoising ECG
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) noise cancellation is essential for accurate analysis and diagnosing of heart conditions. This paper presents an adaptive noise canceller (ANC) designed to remove baseline wandering (BW), electrode motion artifacts (EMAs), and powerline noise (PLN) from ECG signals. Three optimization techniques such as RCGA, DE, and crow search algorithm (CSA) were applied. Comparative analysis revealed that the CSA based ANC achieved superior performance with an SNR out of 89.3364 dB and an MSE of $7.1372 \mathrm{E}-09$, demonstrating enhanced noise reduction and signal clarity. The outcomes validate the effectiveness of this method in enhancing ECG signal quality, supporting more reliable clinical assessments and automated health monitoring systems.

articleTitle: A promising design to enhance the performance of HTL-free and Pb-free PSC
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Since the last few decades, solar cell technology has recorded remarkable advantages over the all-over power of natural power resources. This paper provides the third-generation perovskite-based advanced solar cell. These solar cells overcome the issue of charge recombination, which prompted me to propose a hole transport layer-free (HTL-free) approach in my device. The presence of a lead-based structure renders the device toxic, thus prompting the proposal of a lead-free device. The use of a lower band gap perovskite material yielded better results than the lead-based perovskite material. Applying the work function across the metal contacts completes the charge collection process by creating the proper electric field. The energy alignment must best suit the layers across the PSC; otherwise, it will degrade the efficiency of the PSC. In this particular case, we observed that a work function of 4.085 eV and 4.85 eV yields the best match. This resulted in a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of $\mathrm{1 2. 8 2 \%}$, an open circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.699 V, a fill factor (FF) of 70.84%, and a current density (Jsc) of $25.85 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{cm} 2$. The proposed work will pave the way for future generations to create an interface free from interface defects and hysteresis.

Author Keywords: Charge Transport Layer and Current density

articleTitle: Design and Comparative Analysis of SRM Drive based on Two Novel Power Converter Topologies
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The paper presents, two-novel current control converter topologies for 4-phase Switched Reluctance Motors (SRMs). The first converter is based on a reduced switch model, significantly decreasing the number of switching devices by inducting six IGBT power transistors and three modes of operation for minimizing torque ripple, thus providing a compact, lightweight, and inexpensive design. The second design is based on a MOSFET-switching enhanced four-level converter providing four modes of operation for minimizing torque ripple. Using MATLAB/SIMULINK Software, a 4-phase 8/6 SRM is simulated using the proposed converters. The simulation data validates the torque ripple-reducing capability of the suggested converters in the control process of SRM. Based on simulation outcomes a comparative analysis is performed.

articleTitle: A Finite Control Set based Model Predictive Controller for Load Power Sharing Applications in Inverter Fed Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Microgrids have gained more attention in recent days due to the efficient integration of various distributed energy resources. However, the load power sharing between the distribution generators (DGs) in the microgrids is one of the major challenges, especially at the peak load demand condition. This paper proposes a finite control set-based model predictive controller (FCS-MPC) for the DG-fed inverters in microgrid applications. A universal droop controller model is also considered into account to generate the reference values for the proposed FCS-MPC controller for improved power sharing. The main goal of this paper is to efficiently regulate the power flow from/to the parallel DGs in a microgrid environment. The proposed control method is able to share equal load power, though there is a mismatch in line impedances in the AC microgrid network. In this study, the microgrid test system with two parallel DGs is used to evaluate the performance of the proposed model. To show the effectiveness of the proposed control method, the simulation results of the proposed model have also been compared with the conventional droop control technique. The proposed model has superior performance compared to the conventional droop controller in terms of load power sharing and maintaining tolerance limits, as evidenced by the simulation results.

Author Keywords: Finite Control Set Model Predictive Controller

articleTitle: Enhancement of Ambulatory Monitoring Systems with Active and Passive Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Next-Generation Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of Active and Passive Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (AIRS-PIRS) in moving Ambulatory Monitoring Systems (AMS) within 5G/6G networks. By strategically deploying AIRS-PIRS, electromagnetic waves can be manipulated to enhance signal coverage and quality. The study demonstrates that incorporation of AIRS-PIRS in AMS improves Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) and Bit Error Rate (BER) in Rayleigh fading environment. This research explores both AIRS and PIRS concepts, emphasizing the superiority of joint AIRS-PIRS over single PIRS system in optimizing the AMS performance, that makes AMS more effective for real time health monitoring in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of DC-DC Boost converter using Model Predictive Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A boost converter is a type of device used to convert direct current (DC) from one voltage level to another. It operates by increasing the input voltage to a higher output voltage level.DC-DC converters are utilised in a wide range of applications. The primary application of boost converters is to establish an interface with renewable energy sources.This paper presents a comparative analysis of two controllers, namely the Proportional Integral controller and Model Predictive Control (MPC), for practical applications of the Boost converter. The boost converter is designed and simulated in the MATLAB/SIMULINK environment for this study.The performance of the MPC controller is found to be superior when compared to the PI controller.The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is validated through the utilisation of OPAL-RT.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Direct Refrigerant Cooling Systems for EV Battery Pack
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper examines direct refrigerant cooling systems for prismatic lithium-ion battery packs, offering superior heat dissipation and compact integration compared to traditional air or liquid cooling methods. In these systems, refrigerant directly circulates through the cooling plate, unlike conventional systems where refrigerant cools a secondary coolant. The study analyzes heat transfer dynamics through theoretical calculations, validate predictions and assess real-world performance via experiments, and evaluates the benefits and challenges for electric vehicle (EV) battery management. The findings provide insights into the viability of these systems and guide future advancements in EV thermal management technologies.

articleTitle: On-Board Charger for Electric Vehicles: LLC Resonant Converter Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of control strategies applied to the DC/DC power converter in an On-Board Charger (OBC) for a two-wheeler Electric Vehicle (EV). The analysis is focusssed on the performance and efficiency of the full-bridge LLC resonant converter when governed by Phase Shift Control (PSC) and Model Predictive Control (MPC). Additionally, the OBC features a Power Factor Correction (PFC) stage, managed by an interleaved parallel boost converter with current control to ensure high power quality. he study assesses performance metrics such as converter efficiency and settling time for both control strategies. The OBC for the two-wheeler EV is designed and simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Switched inductor based high gain single switch DC-DC converter
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this paper, a new switched inductor based high gain DC-DC converter is proposed. In the high gain DC-DC converter switched inductor with capacitor that is proposed, switching device and diode combinations used for the realization of switched inductor. In addition, another inductor with diode is presented before the switched inductor. The voltage gain of high gain DC-DC converter is computed. The simulation model of the high gain DC-DC converter is realized using Simpower system block sets of the MATLAB/Simulink plateform. The simulation study of the proposed high gain DC-DC converter is carried. The simulated response shows the efficacy of the high gain converter.

articleTitle: Optimal PMU allocation for system observability considering the effect of Zero-Injection Buses
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) are responsible for monitoring and control actions in a significant number of global power networks; hence, the need for positioning the PMUs in optimal locations has also increased. This paper specifically focuses on the influence of Zero-Injection Buses (ZIBs) on system observability and, in turn, the placing of PMUs. Binary Integer Linear Programming (BILP) is utilized to establish the most effective positions for PMUs across four standard IEEE test systems networks. Also, integration of ZIBs improves the accuracy and reliability of PMU observations in the networks. The results indicate that making strategic PMU allocations while considering ZIBs reduces the total number of PMUs required in some cases. This work provides the basis for planned PMU placement for enhancing the overall reliability of power system monitoring.
