articleTitle: Energy Management in Multi Generator Isolated Microgrid System Using Tyrannosaurus Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Optimal economic power dispatch in microgrids is vital for efficient energy management and cost reduction. The microgrid must meet power demands while maximizing economic benefits. Deploying energy storage with distributed generators stores energy for high load periods. Cost optimization is achieved by strategically dispatching generators and using stored energy during peak loads. The lowest costs are attained when distributed generators run at maximum capacity and battery is used to supply demand during peak intervals when generator capacity is insufficient. The impact of introducing a battery storage system was assessed by equating the operational costs while including and excluding the storage system. An overall saving of 20.79% was achieved by excluding battery storage from the dispatch. The optimal economic dispatch was achieved by incorporating the Tyrannosaurus optimization algorithm (TOA).

articleTitle: Efficient Dual-Hop Routing in Underwater Optical Wireless Networks Using Honey Bee Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Underwater Optical Wireless Networks (UOWNs) offer a promising solution for high-speed data transmission, yet they face significant challenges due to the demanding aquatic environment, which affects signal propagation and data delivery reliability. To enhance UOWN performance, this research introduces an efficient distance-adaptive dual-hop routing method. The Honey Bee Optimization (HBO) algorithm is employed to dynamically select optimal relay nodes and transmission paths, aiming to increase data delivery success rates while minimizing total transmission distances. Simulation results, conducted under varied underwater conditions, demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves network efficiency, reliability, and energy consumption compared to traditional routing algorithms. This approach effectively addresses key challenges, such as signal attenuation and limited communication range, in underwater environments.

articleTitle: A Simple High frequency Model of PMSM Drive with Device Junction Capacitance Effects
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive high frequency model of a PMSM, focusing on the lumped equivalent circuit representation and incorporating significant parasitic capacitances. These capacitances, responsible for leakage currents between motor components, play a critical role in conducted EMI. The detailed parasitic impedance modeling and a high frequency equivalent circuit representation of the motor is given. Using electrostatic analysis, the parasitic capacitances are estimated, and a simplified relationship between high frequency impedance and CMV is established.The analysis extends to include the effect of device junction capacitance (DJC), which becomes significant during switching operations. The DJC contributions, along with the common mode voltage, are incorporated into the model using switching function analysis.By combining the DJC analysis with the high frequency PMSM model, the study provides a complete representation of the drive’s high frequency behavior, offering valuable insights into the leakage current analysis. The analytical expressions are simulated in MATLAB for proper study of CMV and leakage current

Author Keywords: Switching function analysis and High frequency model

articleTitle: Order Reduction for Autonomous LFC Microgrid Systems using Grey Wolf Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper investigates an analysis of load frequency control (LFC) in an autonomous microgrid system. The higher order system (HOS) is reduced to a lower order system (LOS) via order reduction techniques. An $8^{\text {th }}$ order system is reduced to $2^{\text {nd }}$ order model by Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO). The algorithm used is straightforward to implement and doesn’t rely on any controlling parameters. Also, Genetic algorithm (GA), BAT optimization technique and Direct truncation are used to obtain the reduced transfer functions of $2^{\text {nd }}$ order from $8^{\text {th }}$ order microgrid system. The step responses and bode plots are plotted for performance verification. Also, Comparison is provided for the proposed model with HOS and models obtained by other techniques based on time domain specification and error indices.

articleTitle: AI-Based Fault Detection, Classification, and Localization in Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In today’s era of uninterrupted electricity supply is facing significant challenges in fault detection, classification, and precise location of faults in power distribution systems. This paper introduces an innovative methodology utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) techniques to automate fault detection, classification, and location in distribution networks. This paper explores the application of signal analysis, wavelet transform to extract fault signals effectively. These data are analysed and used as input for AI. AI are trained for fault location, leveraging the initial classification results. The integration of AI with Wavelet Transform enables precise detection of fault occurrences, accurate pinpointing of fault locations, and robust classification of fault types. The MATLAB simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in fault management efficiency, showcasing the potential of AI-driven solutions to enhance the reliability and stability of power distribution networks. To evaluate the effectiveness of AI in identifying and managing faults, the proposed system is specifically applied to the Hospital feeder in Maharajgunj, Nepal, a critical infrastructure requiring high reliability. This innovative approach promises to mitigate downtime and optimize maintenance efforts, ensuring uninterrupted power supply to essential services.

articleTitle: Insulator Fault Detection Using Deep Neural Network Based Image Features
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Transmission line insulators are essential parts which ensure power distribution systems are reliable. On the other hand, insulator failures can result in serious issues including power disruptions and inefficient systems. The deep neural network method for identifying insulator problems in transmission lines is presented in this work. The study compares the performance of single-layer and two-layer Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) using a data-set of over 1600 images that are classified into four categories: broken photos, surface defect images, polluted images, and healthy images. The two-layer CNN with a 32-32 neuron configuration achieves the highest accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6. 2 4 \%}$, while the single-layer CNN with 64 neurons attains $\mathbf{9 5. 5 0 \%}$. This research presents the suggested approach, feature selection, and performance analysis, concluding that deep learning models offer significant potential in improving the detection of insulator faults.

articleTitle: Navigating the Smart Grid Landscape: A Comprehensive Review of Recent Advances
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In a world of today, where traditional power systems are being modernized to cater to the evolving needs of the population, the concept of smart grids has become inevitable. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of recent advances in smart grid technologies, focusing on the integration of renewable energy, decentralized control systems, and cybersecurity challenges. Key innovations include microgrids, virtual power plants, and energy storage systems, which collectively enhance grid efficiency and sustainability. The review highlights the role of artificial intelligence and machine learning in optimizing energy distribution, load forecasting, and demand-side management. Additionally, challenges such as bidirectional power flows, cybersecurity threats, and the scalability of digital twins are discussed. Implications for future research emphasize the need for robust regulatory frameworks, scalable energy storage solutions, and advanced cybersecurity measures to support the ongoing evolution of smart grids.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 1MW Grid-Connected Solar Photo Voltaic Plant in India
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive performance analysis of a 1MW grid-connected silicon-polycrystalline (Sipoly) photovoltaic (PV) system utilizing the PVSyst 7.4 simulation tool. The simulation is conducted to achieve optimal energy production. The analysis aims to evaluate efficiency of the system, energy yield, and performance metrics under various conditions. The study provides insights into the operational characteristics, including its energy output, losses, and performance ratio (PR) of the PV system. Simulation is conducted in two phases, the first phase uses adjusting the tilt angle seasonally, while the second phase involves fixed angle throughout the year. The results offer valuable data for optimizing the design and operational strategies of large-scale PV installations Using PVsyst Simulation Tool. Finally simulated data are compared with real time data of the existing PV plant.

articleTitle: Use of L band SAR data together with GPR readings for validation of buried channels in the Jaisalmer region of Rajasthan, India
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: A buried channel is a geomorphic structure, which provides the outline and natural selection of drainage and provide clues to issues concerning the quantity of underground water in the region. SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) data have the potential to unearth the hidden course of lost river channels in the subsurface. This study traces the concealed subsurface river channels buried under the aeolian sediments found 20 km northeast of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan, India using high-resolution ALOS PALSAR-2 SAR data. The results of the study show the existence of buried channels in this region. The mapping of buried channels has been validated by conducting field investigation and the Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) survey. The survey showed the presence of buried sedimentary fluvial deposits in the channels causing high amplitude reflections, which allows us to confirm the existence of buried channels in the study area. The buried channels were delineated using a GPR survey, which supported the results of SAR data. This study has the potential to interpret the subsurface geology and identify placer deposits that are associated with the buried channel, which in turn will help to study the river basin of the semi-arid region.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation and Droop Setting of Droop-Controlled Distributed Generations for Effective Operation of Islanded Microgrid with Solar PV and Wind Generator
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The judicious operation of islanded microgrids is crucial for delivering quality power to consumers reliably. The proper allocation and droop setting of droop-controlled distributed generations play an important role in operating islanded microgrids efficiently and effectively. Thus, in this paper, the optimal allocation of five electronically-coupled distributed generations in an islanded microgrid are obtained by particle swarm optimization method based on a combined objective of minimizing the deviation of the system frequency from the nominal value, the maximum deviation of the node voltage, and system power loss altogether. Now, two optimal distributed generations are replaced by a solar PV module and a wind farm having the same capacities as the corresponding distributed generations. Then, the active and reactive power droop coefficients of the other three droop-controlled distributed generations are optimized for each hour of a day by particle swarm optimization technique based on the same objective considering the variations of loads and generations of solar PV and wind generator. The energy loss, voltage deviation, and the system frequency deviation in the islanded microgrid are reduced for all load conditions of the day by this approach. A 33-node radial islanded microgrid is considered as a test system to illustrate the efficacy of this methodology.

articleTitle: Neural Network based Identification of 3-Φ Battery Energy Storage Systems with Different Capacities
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Microgrids, as self-contained networks within the distribution grid, possess ample distributed generation resources, enabling them to operate independently or in connection with the main grid. However, maintaining stable voltage regulation at each node remains a complex challenge due to fluctuations in generation and load demands. This paper presents a study focused on modeling node voltages using neural networks (NN) for different battery types and capacities connected to a voltage source converter (VSC). The data is derived from an experimental microgrid setup, where active and reactive power regulation is applied at the VSC inputs. By using neural networks, the model predicts local node bus voltage as the output variable, with changes in active and reactive power serving as input variables. This approach allows for a dynamic and responsive voltage control model, addressing the unique operational needs of microgrids. The discussion is given as comparative performance of NN models, optimized using difference of log-sup-exp and Levenberg-Marquardt algorithms.

articleTitle: Accident Liability Assessment Using Traditional Machine Learning Classification Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper focuses on analyzing factors that lead to road accidents, with the main objective of determining if the driver was at fault or not. Road accidents are a major concern that often results in injuries or life-threatening. A considerable amount of these accidents are linked to errors caused by drivers. These errors are generally caused when they engage in nondriving activities which often lead to distractions and increase the chances of accidents. Different parameters are considered to determine the cause of an accident. At the time of the accident, these parameters are collected and they play an important role in determining if it was the driver or other factors responsible for the accident. In this study, we classify accidents by whether they are caused by drivers or by other factors involving them. We assess four machine learning classification models-Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forests, and XGBoost. We identify the most effective method for classifying driver faults by comparing the performance metrics. This paper provides the evaluation of these machine learning classification techniques and aims to give a foremost model for accident liability that could be helpful in contributing to better prevention strategies.

articleTitle: Protecting Substation Differential Relays Against Cyber Attacks Using Convolutional Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The development of digital technology has led to the advancement of electrical power systems and enhanced their reliability and efficiency. With this, the information and communication technology integrated substation devices have made it possible to monitor and control the modern power system smartly. However, all of this comes at the expense of the cyber vulnerability of the power system. The line current differential relays (LCDR) are the most commonly used relays for the protection of transmission lines. LCDR safeguards the lines from faults and could be misused maliciously by the cyber attackers to mal-operate the system. To resolve this issue, this paper introduces a cyber-threat detection system grounded on an unsupervised deep convolutional autoencoder (DCAE) framework, which detects malicious attacks on LCDRs. Remote and local end three-phase current measurements of the protected line with various fault characteristics have been considered to process this. The proposed framework uses fewer features against the existing attack detection methods for LCDRs. The three different scenarios of false data injection attacks (FDIA) have been analyzed at work, and the result shows that the framework achieves higher precision and recall rates with fewer learnt features.

Author Keywords: False data injection attack in differential relays

articleTitle: A Multi - Variate Feature Selection Framework for Comparing Performance of RNN And LSTM For Aspect-Level Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The research addresses the need for automated sentiment analysis (SA) due to the impracticality of manual analysis given the vast amount of online customer feedback. Traditional sentiment analysis methods, which focus on overall sentiment at the sentence or document level, fail to capture detailed insights within customer reviews. To overcome this, the research develops an aspect-level sentiment analysis (ALSA) system using supervised learning techniques. This system aims to identify specific aspects of products or services and evaluate the sentiment expressed towards each aspect, offering a more detailed understanding of customer opinions. The core of the research is a Multivariate Feature Selection Framework for ALSA, which enhances sentiment classification by combining filter and wrapper methods to identify the most relevant features for each aspect. Key components of the framework include Aspect Extraction Using POS tagging and dependency parsing to identify aspects in the text, Feature Extraction for Retaining features that are highly discriminative for aspect-specific sentiment analysis, and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE): Refine the set of features based on its impact on the performance of the machine learning model. The framework is evaluated on benchmark ALSA datasets, showing significant improvements in sentiment classification accuracy over baseline models. It also provides insights into the importance of selected features for different aspects and sentiment polarities, improves accuracy and interpretability, and reduces computational costs by removing redundant features. The ALSA system involves several subtasks, such as extraction of aspects from reviews, extraction of aspects terms, classification of categories, classification of perceived polarity at the aspect level, and calculation of perception score. The approach first extracts aspects and detects sentiment polarity, then extracts relevant features, uses a model for sentiment classification, represents sentiment with a five-point scale, and finally evaluates and calculates the sentiment score. The paper shows a comparison of RNN and LSTM for sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Electrical Systems Using AI-enhanced PUFs
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Cyber-physical systems (CPS) in the electrical domain are becoming increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks, with hardware-level security playing a crucial role in safeguarding their integrity. This paper presents a novel approach that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Physically Unclonable Functions (PUFs) to secure CPS, offering robust, real-time anomaly detection against a range of threats, including side-channel attacks, tampering, and software manipulation. AI-enhanced PUFs leverage intrinsic physical variations in hardware for secure key generation, while AI models improve the detection of anomalies by learning system behaviors under normal and adverse conditions. The methodology proposed involves designing a hybrid PUF architecture and training neural network models to monitor electrical system performance. The AI integration enhances PUF resilience to attacks, adapts to evolving threats, and improves reliability in critical electrical infrastructure. Experimental results can demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in detecting anomalies, offering a promising solution for securing CPS in the electrical sector and beyond.

articleTitle: TCP SYN Flood Attack Detection Using Logistic Regression and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In the realm of cybersecurity, Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks remain a continuous threat, particularly TCP SYN flood attacks due to their stealthiness and potential for disruption. In this paper, we propose a combination of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) with logistic regression for enhancing TCP SYN attack detection, leveraging Actor-Critic as the reinforcement learning algorithm. A novel approach is introduced for hyperparameter optimization using MARL, offering an alternative to traditional techniques such as GridSearchCV and RandomSearchCV. We present a comparative analysis between traditional logistic regression and MARL enhanced approaches, evaluating their performance using metrics such as accuracy, false negatives, and false positives. Results demonstrate that our proposed approach significantly improves detection accuracy and reduces false positives, underscoring its potential in bolstering cybersecurity defenses against sophisticated DDoS threats.

articleTitle: Automated Retinal Disease Detection: VGG16-Based Deep Learning Approach for OCT Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This study aims to develop a robust deep learning model using the VGG16 architecture to accurately classify Retinal OCT images into four categories: CNV, DME, DRUSEN, and NORMAL. The dataset is sourced from Kaggle and consists of 84,495 labeled images that were preprocessed to be $224 \times 224$ pixel size and then convert into 3 channel RGB to make compatible with model. Other data augmentation techniques were used to improve the model’s generalization capability. It split the dataset to training, validation and test subsets, trained the model using these and validated its performance. The results of this model were analyzed in terms of key evaluation metrics, accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and confusion matrix. The model achieved an overall accuracy of $\mathbf{9 5 \%}$ and achieves high precision and recall in all categories, demonstrating its capability for handling class imbalances and complex patterns. Findings of the study showed that the model can be used as an automated diagnostic tool for retinal diseases, providing strong benefits in both clinical and research applications. Future work can extend to deployment of model in real world healthcare settings, integration with multi modal data as a scalable solution for retinal disease detection and management.

articleTitle: Deepfake Detection in Facial Images Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Artificial intelligence achievements in synthetic media synthesis have significantly enhanced the production of ultrarealistic deepfake images that cannot be distinguished from originals. The advancement raises significant concerns about misinformation and invasion of privacy because access to convincingly proficient deepfakes is slowly becoming available. This paper introduces a new approach to detecting deepfakes through the creation of a custom dataset comprising 579,851 images. The dataset is constructed by merging the OpenForensics: Multi-Face Forgery Detection and Segmentation In-TheWild dataset, which contains manipulated images, with a set of AI-generated images. This combination is designed to address recent advancements in AI-generated content. The proposed model then utilizes an eight-layer Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture. The model achieves an accuracy of 84.41%, with a loss value of 0.3484, demonstrating its effectiveness in distinguishing between authentic and AI-generated images. Additionally, a comparative analysis is performed between the proposed model and the CIFAKE image classification model, evaluating both models in terms of performance and efficiency. The analysis highlights the strengths of the proposed solution in detecting AI-generated forgeries. The datasets used in this study, including the OpenForensics dataset and the AI-generated images, are accessible through open-source platforms. AI-generated images were also created using state-of-the-art Stable Diffusion models, ensuring the proposed solution remains adaptable to evolving AI-generation techniques.

articleTitle: Line-to-Ground Fault Analysis in Series-Parallel Connected Solar Photovoltaic Panels Considering Partial Shading Effects
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Solar panels can connect through an array in myriad ways. This research shows the performance for different partial shading conditions through an SP connection for the line-to-ground fault. The SP connection includes extensive, diagonal, inconsistent, flat, core, unshaded, inclined, orthogonal, upright and triangular shading patterns for inspection. The analysis presents the solar array behaviour under shading and fault conditions, which proves that the SP connection attains a maximum efficiency of 13.03% under diagonal shading and a minimum efficiency of $\mathbf{1 0. 6 8 \%}$ under orthogonal shading. Surprisingly, efficiency is not always proportional to the power output. While the extensive shading pattern exhibits the fifth highest efficiency, the lowest power output is experienced. The efficiency rankings in descending order for the connection of SP under line-to-ground fault are diagonal, upright, core, extensive, inconsistent, triangular, flat, inclined, and orthogonal. The software used was MATLAB, with the solar panels used in this array being SPR-220-WHT-U.

articleTitle: Energy Management System for Electric Vehicle Charging Station using Deep Learning and Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The increase of electric vehicles (EVs) necessitates more intelligent infrastructure for charging them. The various energy sources that are available at these EV charging stations would be effectively controlled and monitored by an intelligent energy management system. The main goals would be to arrange EV charging so as to minimize the station’s operational expenses and guarantee that every connected EV receives an adequate amount of charge without impacting the infrastructure. This paper introduces an Energy management system utilizing deep learning and model predictive control. By integrating deep learning for accurate predictions of photovoltaic power and EV demand, this approach addresses uncertainties in load and renewable generation power profiles, ensuring efficient and reliable energy management.

articleTitle: Enhanced EfficientNetB3 Framework for Accurate Multi-Class Eye Disease Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to develop an advanced deep learning model for accurate multi-class eye disease classification, focusing on Cataract, Glaucoma, Diabetic Retinopathy, and Normal conditions. The model uses transfer learning for feature extraction and classification, while leveraging an enhanced EfficientNetB3-based architecture. Utilized a Kaggle dataset comprising 4,217 images, allocating 80% for training and dividing the remaining 20% evenly, with 10% designated for validation and 10% for testing. Data augmentation with random rotations, flips and brightness adjustment was performed to ensure model generalization and reduce model overfitting. The model had an overall accuracy of 95%, and high precision, recall and F1 scores for all classes. The training and validation processes effectively revealed trends in accuracy. Analysis of the confusion matrix also showed minimal misclassifications, and in particular, no misclassifications between overlapping classes, showing the model is reliable. The model’s balanced performance was reinforced by the classification report with macro and weighted averages of 0.94-0.95. Combining transfer learning, data augmentation, and optimized architectures are shown to be important in advancing eye disease detection in this research. The proposed model is a promising model for integration into real time diagnostic tools and mobile applications to detect early and improve clinical decision-making which will ultimately contribute to preventive healthcare strategies.

articleTitle: Bone Age Classification Using Deep Learning: A ResNet50 Model Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The aim of this study was to create and assess a deep learning based automated Bone Age detection model using ResNet50 architecture. Bone age assessment is critical to diagnosing and treating pediatric conditions so our goal was to create a model that could accurately predict bone age from medical images. A transfer learning approach was used to use the pre trained ResNet50 model with a specific task of bone age classification, which was fine tuned. The dataset that was used was 12,611 medical images and were grouped into 8 bone age groups. A confusion matrix was used to show accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, etc. to evaluate the performance on the basis of different age groups and the model was trained and evaluated using standard classification metrics. On average, the model had $\mathrm{9 3. 1 2 \%}$ overall accuracy with very high precision, recall and F1 scores on most classes. The few misclassifications in the confusion matrix demonstrated strong generalization across age groups. This work shows that deep learning models, like ResNet50, can automate bone age assessment. The model performs exceptionally well, potentially making it suitable for use in clinical settings where it could help clinicians make faster, more accurate diagnoses. The results emphasise the utility of applying artificial intelligence in medical imaging for the development of future, more sophisticated, automated diagnostic techniques.

articleTitle: Variable Step Size ZALMS with Optimized PI for Power Quality in Wind Integrated PMSG System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Wind energy generation system will play the best role in supplying power to rural areas without any interruptions, low running cost and fast fault recoveries. Permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) involvement in the system makes it operate at high speeds with low maintenance and it has higher efficiency than other induction generators. Wind integrated PMSG with DSTATCOM device will make an economic power generation system to small rural areas or to make micro-grid. A variable step size least mean square error is selected to improve the convergence of the converter control and to achieve high tracking accuracy in dynamic systems like wind energy power generation systems. The zero attracting concept will attract the higher order components in the system to zero. The variable step size zero attractive least mean square (VSSZALMS) controlled standalone wind integrated power generation system has developed to maintain harmonic free voltage and current at the PMSG terminals under all situations, including imbalanced load currents, load harmonics, and load alterations. Battery energy storage system (BESS) integrated DSTATCOM starts injecting active power into the system to supply required load demand. The PI controller is included in VSSZALMS to maintain terminal voltage at its reference value. Local minimum free, exploration and exploitation involved well optimized African vulture optimization algorithm (AVOA) is selected to tune the PI controller parameters.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Stability Indices in Wind-Integrated Multi-Machines Power Systems Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The main goal of this work is to forecast Transient Energy Conversion (TEC) indicators used to evaluate the security and stability of wind-integrated power systems. Accurate stability assessments are crucial because wind power is intermittent, adding complexity to the system. TEC indices serve as important markers for determining whether a system is stable or unstable. Wind speed and system dynamics fluctuations introduce nonlinear characteristics that standard approaches struggle to handle effectively. Addressing these challenges is vital for ensuring the reliability and security of the electrical grid. Machine learning(ML) algorithms, however, excel in learning from data patterns and adapting to complex, dynamic settings. First, various ML models are tested to predict TEC indicators. Second, polynomial feature transformation with a degree of 2 is applied to capture nonlinearity. Third, hyperparameter tuning is performed using GridSearchCV to optimize model performance. This approach enhances stability evaluation, ensuring the reliability of modern power grids under fluctuating renewable energy conditions.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Prediction Using Artificial Neural Networks: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Diagnostic Accuracy and Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In the last few years, ANN has shown huge promise in predictive healthcare, especially in the diagnosis of breast cancer. This work is therefore devoted to developing and accessing an ANN-based model for the prediction of breast cancer. The dataset contains 569 observations, consisting of radius, texture, perimeter, area, and other measures of smoothness, compactness, and symmetry. These features were used to classify the tumors as either benign or malignant. According to the classification report, an overall accuracy of 96% was achieved by the ANN model. It was supported by an appreciably high precision (96%) and recall (99%) for class 0, which corresponded to a very strong F1-score of 97%. In the case of class 1, malignant, the precision attained was 97, while the recall was as high as 92%, with an F1-score of 95%. The weighted average F 1 -score was 96, hence justifying the model’s strength. The most relevant features that contributed to the accuracy of the model were area mean, perimeter mean, and texture mean. The total dataset contains 32 features that relate to various statistical measures that describe physical characteristics of the tumor. The model's performance underlines the great potential of ANNs in early detection of breast cancer, thereby increasing diagnostic capabilities. The application of such data-driven techniques may enable clinicians to minimize false positives and negatives, which would increase the efficiency of treatment. This study further builds upon the increasing trend of the application of artificial intelligence into clinical use and limits the use of further advanced predictive models in medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: AI-Powered CNC Digital Twin for Predictive Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In today’s manufacturing landscape, maintaining the operational efficiency of CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machines is critical for minimizing downtime and maximizing productivity. This paper presents a novel framework that integrates artificial intelligence (AI) with digital twin technology for predictive maintenance in CNC operations. By leveraging IoT (Internet of Things) sensors, real-time data is collected from CNC machines, enabling the creation of a dynamic digital twin that accurately represents machine performance and behavior. Hereby, employing advanced machine learning techniques, specifically XGBoost, to analyze historical and real-time data, facilitating the early detection of potential failures and optimizing maintenance schedules. It not only enhances the accuracy of maintenance predictions but also significantly reduces the maintenance cost and unplanned machine downtimes. This research contributes to the ongoing development of smart manufacturing systems and underscores the importance of AI-driven solutions in enhancing predictive maintenance strategies within the industrial sector.

articleTitle: PV and Battery Driven Electric Vehicle with SEPIC/ZETA Bidirectional Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The increasing implementation of electric vehicles (EVs) is attributed to the fact that it is possible to reduce the contribution of such vehicles to carbon emissions and fossil fuel dependence. This paper describes a system composed of a PV array, a battery storage unit, and a SEPIC/Zeta bidirectional converter that drives an electric vehicle. To maximize the extraction of solar energy, the PV system is equipped with a boost converter using the Incremental Conductance Maximum Power Point Tracking (INC MPPT) algorithm. This ensures that the EV has full power draw from the PV, in various sun conditions. The SEPIC/Zeta converter also allows for bidirectional power flow because it connects to the battery. This converter is important for the power transfer from the grid or a photovoltaic system to the battery, which is referred to as the buck mode, and to the transfer of power from the battery for vehicle movement, which is known as boost mode. This converter is required in two operational modes; it is charge mode (buck) when doing the grid or PV charging of batteries and also boost mode when making the batteries discharge to drive the EV. By this converter being bidirectional, it can control energy flow in the system to the PV, battery, and EV, thus enhancing the overall system efficiency. This arrangement seeks to enhance energy savings, reduce the need to rely on the grid and support eco-friendly means of transport by integrating cleaner energy with a smart energy management system.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation for GPR Detection of Buried Objects with Varied Sizes and Orientation
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Ground Penetration Radar (GPR) is a remote sensing technology with immense potential. Its performance and quality of results strongly depends on primarily the composition of the soil and further on other aspects of the subsurface targets like the size, material, shape, depth, and orientation. The central operating frequency of the GPR and the type of antenna on the GPR are selected based on the factors above, to be able to detect your intended target satisfactorily. Limited exploratory research work has been undertaken in this field in India towards detection of small shallow buried objects. The present study attempts to experimentally investigate the combined effect of predetermined size and orientation of small shallow buried objects in conjunction with a suitably selected central frequency of the GPR. The experiment was conducted in Jaisalmer, where the arid dry sandy wastelands are conducive to GPR performance. Signal processing methods have been applied to the standard GPR results to derive better output. Apart from the standard effect of material of the targets and the depth buried to, the study mainly provided data indicating a positive correlation between the central operating frequency of the GPR and the quality of detection of the shallow subsurface targets of size corresponding to the wavelength $\lambda$. The positive correlation of polarization of the GPR antenna to the alignment of the buried object was also noted. Further investigations covering more factors affecting GPR performance is advocated by the present study.

articleTitle: Detection of Islanding in AC Microgrid Using Random Forest And Scalogram Image Based Local Binary Pattern
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Islanding is a significant obstacle along with excessive penetration of DG sources. The islanding could cause harm to the customers and their equipment. The IEEE 1547 DG interconnection regulations stipulate that the DG must be disconnected, and the islanding must be observed within two seconds. Basically, this paper presents a novel method for detecting islanding based upon image pattern recognition using random forest (RF) classification technique is proposed. Images are utilized to derive the local binary pattern (LBP) characteristics to identify non-islanding as well as islanding events. Hence, the time series signal is obtained and transformed into scalogram images at the point of common connection. These images are utilized to extract the features using LBP, which is then utilized as a feature vector input for the RF classifier for training as well as testing. It uses the total harmonics distortion (THD) characteristic of the voltage to derive scalogram image. The RF classifier’s effectiveness is assessed with 5 -fold crossvalidations. The result from classification demonstrates that detection of islanding using RF classifier and LBP feature being used for image pattern recognition achieved excellent results with $\mathrm{9 8. 8 9 \%}$ accuracy and detection time of 158 milliseconds.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of A Third-Order Sallen-Key and Multiple Feedback Low Pass Filter for EEG Signal Acquisition System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals are acquired to study the brain-health, brain diseases, and other neuroscience and neuroengineering applications. EEG signals are acquired by an electroencephalography signal acquisition system (ESAS) developed with the amplifier circuit, filter circuit, digitizer, and signal recording circuit. EEG signals are lowamplitude, low-frequency signals which are found very susceptible to interference from noise signals generated by motion artifacts, power sources, electrodes, and external factors. In an analog circuit of a neural potential acquisition system, we aim to amplify the signal with minimal power consumption at minimized noise level. Simultaneously it will lower the frequency spectrum so that only desired signal targetted is passed and other unwanted signals called noises are filtered out. The low-power circuit design is essential to minimize the power consumption, heat dissipation, and noise generation to ensure the high signal-to-noise ratio as well as to avoid the failure which might harm surrounding tissues. The current study innovates in developing a sophisticated low-pass filter with power reduction for recording epileptic signals. A thirdorder low-pass filter (LPF) is suggested whose design minimizes its transconductance at the nanoscale using the Sallen-Key (SK) and Multiple Feedback (MFB) topologies. The proposed architecture achieves a mid-band gain of 50.2 dB and a - $\mathbf{3 d B}$ bandwidth that extends from 20 Hz to 500 Hz. Simulation results were obtained in a NI Multisim environment.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Efficiency of Lead-Less Cs2 TiBr6 Solar Cells through Dual Hole Transport Layer Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Abstract-The potential of lead-free perovskite solar cells (PSCs) has garnered prominent interest, particularly due to concerns surrounding the toxicity and instability of lead halide compounds. Enhancing the performance of lead-free, ecologically friendly PSCs utilizing the perovskite absorber layer (PAL) Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> TiBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, is the goal of this endeavor. This simulation investigation reveals comprehensive findings from particular modeling techniques for PSCs. The proposed study incorporates an innovative dual-hole transport layer (HTL) to enhance the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the device. The PSC achieves the highest PCE by combining two HTLs, notably Copper Antimony Sulfide (CuSbS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and Copper Barium Thiostannate (CBTS). The proposed device structure, $\mathrm{FTO} / \mathrm{TiO}_{2} / \mathrm{Cs}_{2} \mathrm{TiBr}_{6} / \mathrm{CuSbS}_{2} / \mathrm{CBTS} / \mathrm{Ni}$, is analyzed using SCAPS-1D simulations to compare and optimize key parameters, including energy band alignment, current-voltage ($\mathrm{J}-\mathrm{V}$), and quantum efficiency (QE) properties, absorber and transport layer thickness, parasitic resistances, interface defects, and temperature. Our findings reveal that the dual HTL configuration performs better than previously cited single HTL-based structures. The proposed $\mathrm{Cs}_{2} \mathbf{T i B r}_{6}$-based PSC structure improves the device’s photovoltaic (PV) parameters, achieving an enhanced open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.34 V, a short-circuit current density ($\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{SC}}$) of $21.28 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$, and a fill factor FF of $\mathbf{8 6. 2 4 \%}$, culminating in PCE of $\mathbf{2 4. 6 4 \%}$. This research demonstrates the efficacy of employing dual HTLs in enhancing the performance and stability of PSCs, providing promising insights for the future advancement of high-efficiency PV devices.

articleTitle: EV Charging Station Integrated Microgrid Planning by Using Fuzzy Adaptive DE Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Due to environmental concerns, renewable energy has gained significant popularity over the past two decades. Integrating distributed generation and renewable energy sources, particularly through microgrids in power distribution systems, has become feasible. Additionally, there has been a notable increase in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) driven by environmental initiatives and their advantages over internal combustion engines. As a result, the planning and operation of microgrids in distribution systems have become more complex. To address these complexities, computational evolutionary algorithms have emerged as effective solutions. The Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm stands out for its speed and userfriendly simplicity. The proposed study uses the Fuzzy Adaptive Differential Evolution (FADE) analysis for microgrid planning integrated with EV charging infrastructure, using the IEEE 33bus system. The FADE algorithm combines the power of fuzzy logic and adaptive strategies within the DE framework to tackle the planning and optimization challenges of microgrids integrated with Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS). The findings provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of the FADE algorithm in addressing the challenges associated with the planning and operation of microgrids with EVCS in modern power systems.

Author Keywords: Fuzzy Adaptive Differential Evolution optimization algorithm

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based Recommendation System: An In-Depth Review of Models and their Limitations
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper surveys the landscape of the Al model approaches and algorithms that have been in use in recommendation systems, which have become an essential requirement in enriched user experiences, ranging from e-commerce to content streaming and social media, among other areas. We focus on a few remarkable techniques: Multi-Armed Bandit, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), Deep Q-Network (DQN), Proximal Policy Optimization, and Twin Delayed DDPG. Every model is discussed in detail for the purpose of demarcating the merits and demerits, besides shedding light on some major findings of past literature. We enumerate some important research gaps in the domain that relate to scalability, adaptability to dynamic user preferences, and context-awareness. We aim to highlight the potential and limitations of these algorithms across various applications, proposing directions for future research to improve recommendation systems.

articleTitle: Exploring the Influence of Kesterites as Hole Transport Layers in Cs2TiBr6-Based Eco-Friendly Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Lead-free, eco-friendly perovskites have gained significant attention for their non-toxicity, addressing environmental concerns while enhancing the sustainability of photovoltaic (PV) technologies and maintaining high power conversion efficiency (PCE). Through detailed numerical simulations this study investigates the impact of kesterite materials as hole transport layers (HTLs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), utilizing Caesium Titanium Bromide (Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>TiBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>) as the perovskite absorber layer (PAL) and Titanium Dioxide $\left(\mathrm{TiO}_{2}\right)$ as the electron transport layer (ETL). The objective is to enhance performance, and stability and reach a PCE greater than $\mathbf{2 5 \%}$. Various kesterite compounds, including copper zinc tin selenide (CZTSe), copper manganese tin sulphide (CMTS), copper iron tin sulphide (CFTS), copper nickel tin sulphide (CNTS), copper zinc tin sulphide (CZTS), and copper barium tin sulphide (CBTS), were analyzed to evaluate their effectiveness as HTLs. Using the SCAPS-1D tool, key factors such as band alignment, optimal layer thickness, and current-voltage (J-V) characteristics, along with quantum efficiency (QE), were evaluated to identify the most effective HTL. Additional simulations investigated the impact of series resistance ($\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{s}}$), shunt resistance (Rsh) and temperature on device performance. The findings demonstrated that CZTSe outperformed other kesterites as HTL due to its superior absorption coefficient, favorable band alignment, and higher charge carrier formation and extraction capabilities. The configuration resulted in an open-circuit voltage ($V_{O C}$) of 0.78 V, a short-circuit current leading to an overall PCE of $\mathbf{2 5. 3 6 \%}$. These findings highlight the potential of CZTSe as a promising HTL for high-PCE, leadfree PSCs, advancing sustainable solar technology.

articleTitle: Advanced Energy Management Strategies for Hybrid Energy Storage Systems in Electric Vehicles: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: An increasing need for sustainable transportation and the emergence of system HESS (hybrid energy storage systems) with supercapacitors and batteries have motivated the research and development of electric vehicles (EVs). In this review paper, different energy management strategies implemented in HESS for electric vehicles are investigated for improved efficiency and performance. The main goal is to compare some control methods like fuzzy logic control, model predictive control and genetic algorithms and to evaluate their performance in the optimization of the energy distribution among storage components. This study brings together multiple research articles to offer a complete review of these strategies. It is found from key findings that fuzzy logic control is adaptable to different driving conditions and model predictive control consistently provides precise domestic energy management with the aid of sophisticated predictive algorithms. In contrast, genetic algorithms excel at optimizing complex, multi objective problems; but at a large computational cost. In summary, it is shown that these advanced control strategies can be combined to combine high energy efficiency and long-life spans of HESS systems in electric vehicles. Some valuable insights are provided which could be useful reference for research in future as well as development in this field. This review seeks to help researchers and engineers select and refine energy management strategies that enable more sustainable and efficient electric transportation solutions.

articleTitle: Application of Intelligent Techniques in Smart Grid Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The smart grid is an advanced power system network that integrates cutting-edge technologies to enable efficient, reliable, and sustainable energy generation, distribution, and utilization. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of intelligent techniques, including machine learning for load forecasting and fault detection, optimization algorithms for demand-side management and renewable energy integration, and data analytics for real-time grid monitoring and decisionmaking. These approaches enhance grid performance by improving flexibility, operational efficiency, and resilience to disruptions. Specific examples, such as predictive maintenance using machine learning and optimization-based energy scheduling for microgrids, are discussed to illustrate their practical applications. The paper also explores challenges like cybersecurity and data quality, offering potential mitigation strategies. Additionally, successful implementations and their outcomes are highlighted, showcasing the transformative impact of intelligent techniques on smart grid automation. Finally, future research directions, such as leveraging blockchain for secure transactions and quantum computing for advanced optimizations, are identified to guide advancements in this field.

articleTitle: Prediction of Remaining Useful Life in MEMS Devices Using a Stacking Model Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Accurate estimation of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) devices is essential for enhancing predictive maintenance in industrial settings. This paper proposes a robust stacking ensemble model for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of MEMS devices, integrating sensor and mechanical component data. Publicly available RUL datasets were augmented using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), ensuring diverse input data. Key al-gorithms-Bayesian Ridge, Random Forest, and XGBoost-were identified using Lazy Predict and combined with a Support Vector Regressor (SVR) as the meta-learner. Hyperparameter optimization was performed using the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm, offering enhanced efficiency for large datasets and dynamic retraining. The model demonstrated superior performance based on RMSE and $\mathbf{R}^{2}$ metrics compared to traditional methods. Deployment was achieved via a Flask web application integrated with a CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions and Docker, ensuring scalability and reproducibility. This research contributes a scalable and efficient framework for advancing predictive maintenance in industrial automation.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis in AC Microgrids Using Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and Kernel-Based Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: As the global energy landscape transitions towards sustainability, decentralized power generation through AC microgrids plays a crucial role in reducing transmission losses and integrating renewable energy sources (RES) like solar and wind. While RES offers environmental benefits, their intermittent nature presents significant challenges to the reliability and stability of microgrids. Accurate fault detection and classification are essential in addressing these challenges, but traditional threshold-based methods often fail to cope with the dynamic and non-linear behavior of microgrids. This paper introduces a novel fault detection and classification method for AC microgrids that combines Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT) for feature extraction with a kernel-based Support Vector Machine (SV Machine) classifier. By analyzing timeseries data from phase currents and utilizing an SV Machine with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel, the proposed method effectively identifies multiple fault types in real time. Simulation results demonstrate that the kernel-based SV Machine model with an RBF kernel achieves an impressive accuracy of 98.14%, along with high precision and recall, highlighting its robustness in practical applications. This study underscores the potential of kernel-based algorithms in enhancing the sustainability and reliability of modern energy systems. The innovative combination of STFT and SV Machine sets a new standard for advanced fault detection in decentralized power systems, making it a powerful tool for the future of energy management.

articleTitle: Application Deployment: The Game-Changing Impact of Containerization
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This study will introduce the use of Docker for simple application packaging to investigate the impact of packaging on application deployment and management. Containerization is a technological method for packaging and consuming applications in a self-contained environment that is more efficient than virtualization. Docker is a well-known containerization platform that enables efficient creation, deployment, and management of applications by focusing and efficiently utilizing resources across multiple locations. Delivering programs and investigating their similarities in terms of consistency, efficiency, and effectiveness. It also solves security issues and multi-container issues. The approach will be to package a simple web application, deploy it via Docker, and then measure how performance and manageability are improved compared to traditional deployments. Using Docker for application deployment helps you better understand how containerization can improve and simplify deployment and management in today’s software development.

articleTitle: Precise Fault Distance Prediction in Distributed Generators-Integrated Transmission Lines Using CNN-LSTM Ensemble Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Precise fault distance estimation is critical for effective transmission system protection, especially in modern power systems with integrated distributed generators (DGs). As the global demand for energy continues to rise, the adoption of renewable energy sources and their integration into the grid has significantly increased. However, the presence of various DGs complicates fault distance estimation due to the diverse power flows and interactions between DGs and existing grid infrastructure. The integration of large-scale DGs introduces additional challenges in fault detection and location, as the dynamic behavior of these generators affects the fault characteristics. This paper focuses on precise fault distance estimation within the IEEE-9 bus system, which includes two distinct DGs. The proposed solution leverages an ensemble deep learning approach, combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. This hybrid CNN-LSTM model takes advantage of CNN’s ability to extract spatial features and LSTM’s strength in capturing temporal dependencies, making it well-suited for fault distance prediction. The model’s performance is evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), giving 0.6387 average MAE for the studied system. Comparative analysis with existing deep learning models and validated through OPAL-RT 4510 real-time simulator shows that the proposed model delivers superior performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling the complexities introduced by DG integration.

articleTitle: Fault Localization Technique in Smart Active Distribution System with Data Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The necessity for a reliable power supply in active distribution systems requires information on precise fault location to restore the power following a fault. However, with inverter based DGs the modulated voltage and current limits the faulty section and fault location technique. Smart grid initiatives have added Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) and SCADA systems through communication networks which collects large sets of data which improves the monitoring of the whole system and this can also be applicable to obtain the fault location. However, the existence of errors in data presents a notable obstacle in locating the faults. Hence, to estimate the accurate data, weighted least squares and the chi-square probability density function-based approach are applied and with accurate estimated data, faulty line inductance is computed using the least squares (LSQ) technique. The proposed method is highly accurate for data uncertainties, high resistance fault, and bidirectional power flow. Further, the method is compared with a Current distribution technique (CDT) based impedance/ reactance fault location method, which is beneficial for close-infault. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated through simulation of the IEEE 33-bus Distribution System using MATLAB/SIMULINK R2023a.

articleTitle: ANN-Based Switch Fault Detection and Localization in 3-Φ Five Level T-Type Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents an effective open circuit (OC) fault detection and faulty switch localization in a three-phase five-level T-Type inverter (3-ø 5-LT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> I), with the added benefit of identifying the faulty phase. The three-phase system involves of three single-phase units, each with a 120 -degree phase shift. This topology employs a data-driven approach to detect and identify faulty switches. Under this method, Phase and line voltages are used as raw input data, from which root mean square (RMS) values are calculated under various single-switch fault conditions across different phases. These RMS values are then fed into an Artificial Neural Network (ANN), which analyzes the dataset to determine if a switch is faulty and, if so, identifies the specific faulty switch and its corresponding phase. Additionally, the proposed topology naturally maintains selfvoltage balancing in the DC link capacitor and operates with a single DC source. Extensive simulation studies are carried out to assess the efficiency and robustness of this approach.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Kernel Methods in Quantum Support Vector Machines for Network Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In cybersecurity space, accurate and efficient identification of network anomalies is crucial in protection of information systems and data. The purpose of this research is to present QSVM for improving the detection of anomalies in network traffic using the NSL-KDD dataset. The work uses QSVM and applies different kernel functions such as a linear kernel, a polynomial kernel, a radial basis function (RBF) kernel, and a sigmoid kernel to analyze the effects on QSVM. The degree to which each kernel can draw decision boundaries is plotted, which offers an understanding of how well the paradigm performs in identifying networks anomalies. Quantum computing is a useful application as it provides means for the improvement of the limiting factors of involving machine learning in security, and this work could help increase the efficiency of the realized methods in detecting anomalies. The outcomes of this research study are believed to stimulate more study of the interaction between quantum computing and network security

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Drowsiness Detection Systems for Enhanced Road Safety Across Diverse Vehicle Types
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper proposes the development of multiple driver drowsiness detection systems to enhance road safety across different types of vehicles, including two/three-wheelers, cars, and commercial trucks. The research encompasses three primary components: an initial prototype, a wearable device model, and a webcam-based model. The prototype utilizes infrared (IR) sensors to detect driver blinking patterns, activating an alarm and gradually stopping the vehicle when drowsiness is detected. The wearable device model effectively integrates IR sensors into helmets and glasses, making it a cost-effective and efficient solution for two/three-wheelers, which are prone to higher accident rates. The webcam-based model employs computer vision and machine learning techniques, using parameters such as Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR), Mouth Aspect Ratio (MAR), and excessive yawning to detect drowsiness. If drowsiness is detected, the system sends live location messages to emergency contacts. This model also features app support for real-time analysis of driver performance, benefiting both personal use and commercial monitoring of truck operators transporting hazardous goods. Our findings suggest that these models provide a versatile and impactful approach to reducing road traffic accidents.

articleTitle: Integrative Automation of Cybersecurity Systems through Advanced Data Science Methodologies: Enhancing Predictive Analytics and Real-Time Threat Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Due to emergence in Corona disease, the digital revolution become more intensified which makes more prevalent in day-to-day activities. As a result, cloud service providers become more frequent. Therefore, system integration is essential throughout a partner ecosystem. Unbelievably many edge devices are sending IoT data to the cloud. The system becomes automated due to the organizational structures which resulted in developing new technologies. This new” Integration ecosystem” is where there is just one platform forall the system. According tothe survey of 4,500 decisionmakers, data protection—rather than business process optimization or processautomation—was the primary argument for employing AI within organizations. Using ML algorithmsto automatically identify cyberattacks is referred to as automating cyber security systems. By leveraging automation, cyber security systems can swiftly identify and respond to attacks, reducing the amount of time needed to avert possible harm. With the considerations in mind, we proposed Automating Cyber Security Systems with Data Science Practices in which we will be talking about how various cyber security systems can effectively utilize current data science practices to automate their workflow.

articleTitle: State of Health Estimation of Lithium-ion Batteries Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are an important component in applications such as electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and consumer electronics due to their high efficiency and high energy density. Accurate State of Health $(\mathbf{S o H})$ prediction is critical to ensure battery performance, safety, and longevity. Traditional methods often struggle to capture the complex nonlinear relationships inherent in battery behavior. This paper investigates the use of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and their variants, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) for SoH computation. The comprehensive datasets are collected in the battery parameters, including voltage, current, temperature, and capacity. These data were preprocessed to address noise and inconsistencies of the lithium-ion batteries. RNN models, including LSTM and GRU, were trained and evaluated using the preprocessed dataset. The performance of the models was assessed based on metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and R-squared (R2). The results show that RNN algorithms capture the non-linearities of battery parameters well, improving SoH prediction accuracy. For example, the RNN model achieved the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE) of $\mathbf{0. 0 0 0 0 1 4}$ and the highest $\mathbf{R 2}$ of 0.974455 for the $\mathbf{B 4 6}$ cells, demonstrating its robustness and accuracy. This study highlights the potential of deep learning algorithms to enhance battery management systems (BMS) and extend the service life of lithium-ion batteries.

articleTitle: Diabetic Retinopathy Detection Using InceptionV3: A Deep Learning Approach for Automated Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This study focuses on implementing InceptionV3, a deep learning model to classify DR into five stages: The different categories are: No DR, Healthy, Mild DR, Moderate DR, Proliferative DR and Severe DR. The data split is based on the Kaggle’s Diabetic Retinopathy Dataset, which has 2,750 coloured images of the retina with dimensions of $224 \times 224$ pixels after using resizing, normalization and augmentation techniques to prevent model overfitting as well as data imbalance. The entire data set was divided into three groups: training, validation, and testing to enhance the generalization of the outcomes. The proposed model obtained an overall accuracy of 95.75% and high precision, recall, and F1-measure for the majority of the classes. The Healthy and Moderate DR classes showed nearly comparable performance, whereas the detection of the Proliferative and Severe DR classes remained a challenge owing to class imbalance. Metrics used for evaluating the model, such as accuracy, confusion matrix and classification report, showed us the areas of success and failure of the model. Further study will be directed towards the enhancement of the minority classes by employing data augmentation together with investigating the effectiveness of multi-modal data. These techniques of explainable AI are expected to improve the interpretability for clinical use. This work identifies a viable and efficient approach for automated DR detection that may help improve diagnostic capabilities in ophthalmology.

articleTitle: Integrated decision support framework architecture for rolling stock maintenance management - sustainable software perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper proposes a decision support framework architecture designed to optimize fleet management, particularly focusing on minimizing total maintenance costs. The framework includes a planning optimization module, which integrates input data, a mathematical model, and optimization methods to develop cost-effective schedules for locomotives assigned to transport tasks. Through the application of various optimization algorithms, including simulated annealing, genetic algorithms, and their cost versions, the case study demonstrates substantial cost reductions on average by more than thirty percent compared to basic approaches. The results highlight the framework’s capability to support strategic decision-making in fleet composition, contract evaluation, and maintenance planning. Energy-saving algorithms, modular structure and optimization of resources make the framework sustainable software.

articleTitle: Weather Image Recognition Based on Convolutional Neural Network and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper introduces a groundbreaking approach to weather phenomena classification, presenting a novel deep neural network design (Resnet 50 with transfer learning). Simultaneously, we present the creation of a comprehensive dataset named the Weather Database, comprising 50,000 images featuring four distinct weather phenomena expanding the categorization beyond previous datasets. By broadening the scope of categorized weather phenomena and leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, our approach contributes to advancing accurate and efficient weather recognition systems, thereby enhancing the overall reliability of weather forecasting processes. Through rigorous testing, our proposed model (Resnet 50) demonstrates a notable result accuracy of approximately $\mathbf{9 1. 5 6 \%}$ on the testing set. In the model by incorporating the advanced metrics and analytical techniques, the evaluation process will transcend basic accuracy assessments, providing a more comprehensive perspective on the model’s capabilities. The accuracy, training time etc of the proposed model with conventional CNN model & SVM model have been compared and it is concluded that the proposed one is superior. This research also presents a method for conducting a comprehensive review of existing literature on other analytical approaches applied to weather forecasting. Here, Python 3.11 software and MATLAB 2023 have been used throughout the paper to carry out the simulation task.

articleTitle: DenseNet201-Powered Dental Radiograph Classification: A Deep Learning Approach for Multi-class Dental Pathology Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this study, the automated dental radiograph classification problem was addressed by a deep learning approach using DenseNet201 architecture. The research utilized a comprehensive dataset of 29,815 dental X-ray images across five categories: 69.0%, fillings (20.3%), implants (6.9%), cavity (2.1%), and impacted teeth (1.7%). To tackle class imbalance, the dataset was pre-processed with resizing to 224 x 224 pixels, normalization, and data augmentation techniques. 85.3% of the data were used for training, 9.1% for validation, and 5.6% for testing. With ImageNet weights and using Adam optimizer, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 91%. Performance analysis revealed excellent results for normal cases (F1-score: 0.95) and implants (F1-score: 0.91), while cavity detection showed lower performance (F1-score: 0.27) due to limited samples. While showing the capabilities of deep learning in dental radiography classification, the study also identifies where deep learning can improve on minority class detection. Finally, future work is proposed to incorporate attention mechanisms and increase the dataset to improve diagnostic accuracy in clinical applications.

articleTitle: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) for Manufacturing Technology in Industry 4.0: The Possibilities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is a computerized tomographic (CT) technique which provides a cross-sectional image of an object under test in terms of its electrical impedance distribution. In EIT an array of surface electrodes with an electronic instrumentation is used to collect the boundary voltage current data by conducting complete scanning with electrical current or voltage signal similar to the X-Ray beam scanning done in X-Ray CT. Spatial distribution of electrical impedance is reconstructed from the measured boundary data using a computer program called image reconstruction algorithm. As a non-invasive radiation free tomographic imaging modality EIT finds a lot of applications in several practical problems in engineering and technology. In industrial engineering, material products are possible to assess using EIT and hence a number of manufacturing problems are studied using EIT. The present paper presents a brief review of the application of EIT in manufacturing technology and summarizes its possibilities and challenges followed by recent trends in industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Agriculture Waste and Bioenergy: A Content Analysis Review and Visualization
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The rising demand for sustainable energy has increased interest in bioenergy. The primary source of bioenergy is agricultural waste, which offers an environmentally friendly alternative to fossil fuels. The review provides an inclusive analysis of the current agricultural waste and bioenergy literature and emphasizes vital trends, technologies, and challenges. It utilized Vosviewer software to identify key themes and research trends using author keywords, index keywords, and all keywords. 885 Scopus-indexed documents were analyzed. The results reveal that the most recurrently occurring keywords are “bioenergy,” “biomass,” and “agriculture,” which indicates a strong focus on sustainable energy production. The terms “anaerobic digestion,” “biogas,” and “biofuels” emerge as leading technologies. A cluster analysis of 88 phrases revealed three significant research clusters in the title and five in the abstract fields, indicating a wide range of pivotal areas. Despite tremendous progress, there are still gaps in understanding specific kinds of agricultural waste and novel bioenergy technologies, such as microbial fuel cells.
