This review offers valuable insights into current research trends, opportunities, and future directions for agricultural waste and bioenergy, strongly emphasizing sustainability and technological innovation.

articleTitle: Cyber Security in Smart Grid- A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The smart grid (SG) relies on a diverse array of communication methods to facilitate bi-directional data exchange. These methods encompass wired connections, optical fibers, and wireless technologies. Furthermore, communication functionalities are classified according to their specific purposes, including sensing, telecommunications, and control. However, the intricate interconnectedness of these communication networks introduces vulnerabilities, increasing the risk of cyber-attacks. The dense web structure of the SG system means that any component may be susceptible to intrusion or manipulation by malicious actors. Ensuring the security of the SG infrastructure hinges on the accurate evaluation of the efficacy of existing security mechanisms. This necessitates a comprehensive understanding of potential threats and vulnerabilities. Therefore, this study aims to provide detailed insights into the types of cyber-attacks that could potentially compromise the integrity and functionality of the SG system.

articleTitle: Evaluating Lightweight Asymmetric Cryptography for Secure Communication in Internet of Drones
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are being successfully used in a variety of applications, including agriculture, search and rescue operations, surveillance systems, and mission-critical services, thanks to some technological and practical advantages, such as high mobility, the ability to extend wireless coverage areas, or the capacity to reach locations inaccessible to humans. In contrast, attacks against drones, as opposed to traditional cyberattacks, typically happen as a result of serious design flaws and a lack of wireless security protection methods. The study examines lightweight asymmetric cryptographic algorithms for secure Internet of Drones (IoD) communication, addressing cybersecurity challenges within this emerging technology. It evaluates RSA, ElGamal, Diffie-Hellman, and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), focusing on their suitability for IoD through comparative analysis of calculation time, memory usage, key size, and security. The goal is to contribute to developing robust, efficient, and secure communication protocols for IoD, promoting growth while mitigating risks. This research is pivotal for the advancement of IoD security, exploring the application of these cryptographic techniques to ensure secure, efficient operations within the IoD framework.

articleTitle: 3DAES: An Ensemble of Symmetric cryptographic protocol for Data security
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In this digital world, data plays a significant role, and protecting these data is required. Cryptographic protocols are employed for encryption of data sent between sender and recipient. To transfer data specifically between known sender and receiver faster and more securely, the symmetric protocol is better than the asymmetric one. The real issue with symmetric is to share the secret key securely with the receiver from the sender. Also, specific protocols have certain mathematical flaws which decrease their security. So in this paper, an asymmetric key transfer mechanism is proposed, an ensemble of 2 symmetric protocols, AES-128 and 2DES-inspired algorithms. This protocol uses Diffie Hellman-based key exchange to transfer the symmetric key among the receivers asymmetrically. This makes the data transfer secure and faster.

articleTitle: Logic OR Based Forward Backward Load Flow Method for DG Placement and Sizing with Modified Fuzzy Max-Min Principle for Different Load Types
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant concentration of distributed generation (DG) resources due to their positive impact on the electrical system. However, research has shown that improper placement and sizing of DG units can lead to increased losses and negatively affect the voltage profile. To mitigate these issues, careful consideration and strategic planning are necessary when integrating DGs into the distribution network (DN). For DNs with high resistance-to-reactance (R/X) ratios, traditional Newton Raphson Load Flow (NR-LF) approaches are inappropriate because of the singularity of the Jacobian matrix. In order to overcome this, an improved and Modified Forward Backward Load Flow (MFB-LF) method which is based on straightforward matrix equations is put into practice and effectively tested for the load flow analysis on distribution networks. The multi-objective optimization challenge is tackled through the application of the Mixed Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization (MD-PSO) method, enhanced with the Modified Fuzzy max-min principle. The proposed technique is verified on a 33-bus DN under various load scenarios. By testing under diverse load types, the technique’s ability to reduce power losses and improve voltage profiles is thoroughly evaluated.

Author Keywords: DG placement for different load types

articleTitle: Transforming Ophthalmology: A CNN-Based Mechanism for Diabetic Retinopathy Screening
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a solemn eye ailment that can root vision loss if not diagnosed. It is a complication of diabetes and is caused when high blood sugar destroys the retina. While DR cannot be reversed, early detection and treatment can prevent or slow down vision loss. Traditional physical prognosis of DR by ophthalmologists can be inefficient, prone to errors, and expensive. Computer-aided finding systems, especially those using deep learning mechanisms, have produced great promise by enhancing the accuracy of DR recognition. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are a particular kind of deep learning mechanism that has been highly successful in analyzing medical images. In this study, we achieved a 95% accuracy in detecting DR using a CNN-based approach.

articleTitle: Enhanced Quantum Key Distribution Protocol for Secure Smart Grid Communication using Quantum Gates
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocol to strengthen the security of smart grid systems through secure communication and signature verification. As smart grids increasingly depend on digital communication, safeguarding them against cyber threats is paramount. Our approach incorporates Hadamard, SWAP, and rotation gates to fortify the BB84 protocol, ensuring secure key exchange while verifying the integrity and authenticity of transmitted data between smart meters and grid operators. Experimental results demonstrate that the protocol provides efficient key generation, encryption, and decryption while improving eavesdropping detection. With 10 qubits, the protocol achieved a key generation rate of 957 bits and successfully encrypted messages. These findings suggest that QKD offers a robust security framework for smart grid environments, providing superior resistance to both quantum and classical attacks.

articleTitle: Protection Challenges in Photovoltaic Systems: A Review of Recent Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The protection issues with photovoltaic (PV) systems which are crucial for producing sustainable energy are thoroughly reviewed in this work. Unidirectional power flow, fault isolation and detection, inverter protection, overvoltage and overcurrent, arc faults, islanding, defense against lightning and surges, and integration with current grid systems are among the main concerns. The effectiveness and security of PV systems may be jeopardized by the particular dangers associated with each of these issues. The review focuses on new developments that tackle these issues, such as improved inverter protection techniques and sophisticated failure detection systems. These developments in technology are essential for enhancing PV systems dependability and security and facilitating the switch to renewable energy sources. The key findings highlight how crucial it is to conduct continuous research and development in order to improve these safeguards and guarantee the long-term viability of solar energy systems in a sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Advancing Waste Classification for Sustainable Recycling: A Deep Learning Approach Using VGG-16
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The study is necessary to categorize wastes more precisely and efficiently into organizations, resulting in less environmental demeaning, and it can also foster recycling processes. The research study is intended to present a robust deep learning-based model for categorizing wastes into “Organic” and “Recyclable” classes on behalf of auto waste sorting systems. The dataset used for this work has been taken from Kaggle, labeled 25,077 images, which were divided into a training set and a test set. The images were first pre-processed and prepared for model input through resizing, converting to RGB, and standardizing data. Transfer learning was applied here; the architecture of VGG-16 in this case was taken as a feature extractor with additional dense layers along with dropout and batch normalization for regularization. Early stopping considers preventing overfitting and allows the model to maintain optimal weights. The model achieved a high accuracy of 91%, while the precision and recall for the two categories were well-balanced, as evidenced by the classification report and confusion matrix. Such an excellent performance anchors the proof that the model is indeed capable of making high-accuracy distinctions between Organic and Recyclable waste types and hence suitable for any real-world application. Implications of this work: improved sorting accuracy, reduction in man-hours, and waste management in a sustainable manner. The future work may focus on enhancing the model performance by adding more regularization, augmentation techniques, and ensemble learning into the system so that more types of waste could be classified to carry out useful tasks, which would be very useful to accelerate intelligent waste management.
